[02:33:42] — he is in the man's face. there is no travel in between. one frame at the door, one frame at the chair.

[02:33:44] "hey. do you have a family?"

[02:33:46] "wh— wha— i, yeah, bu—"

[02:33:47] "shhhh. oh my god. rhetorical question. you do! i know you do!"

[02:33:52] "a mom. a dad. and a wife sick at home with, what was it again… oh, yeah, right! the poison you gave her. because youre a sick piece of shit. youre not gonna be in her will, man."

pinned post. first entry. read this one before anything else on the site.

entry 000wk 1 · 02:17

i shoot scenes for coin. off book, freelance. i sell stills to fixers, and sometimes a corp wants proof a job actually happened. ive seen a lot of rooms with dead people in them. i dont usually write about it.

this one is different. four scenes in three months that shouldnt connect and do. same fire pattern. same nobody-heard-anything. same twenty seconds of static on the hideout comm before it clicks over to a station that doesnt exist on any registered frequency ive been able to find.

i started keeping notes because the details wouldnt sit still in my head. this site is those notes, cleaned up enough to read. i dont have a name. i dont have a clean face. i have what he leaves behind, and it is starting to add up to something i cant just hand off to a fixer and forget about.

if you know him, dont reach out to me about it. i mean that.

— relay

edit much later: left this entry exactly as written even though the last line aged into a joke. people reached out. i answered every one of them. of course i did.
tagged: start here 2 comments
entry 000.1 // addendumrelay

nine days later and i still havent slept right.

use the nav up top. logs are the raw scene notes. chrome and arsenal are what ive pieced together about what hes running. witnesses is testimony, not mine. signal is the one that actually matters. terminal is something i shouldnt have and am not going to explain how i got. board is where i keep trying to make it all connect on paper because it stopped fitting in my head. guestbook is open, for now.

entry 000.2 // laterwk 10 · 05:03

im not sleeping right and i want to be honest about that up front, because it matters for how you read everything after this point.

i caught myself doing something last week i havent told anyone. a new scene came in that matched three things i predicted in the chrome section before i even walked in the door. for about four seconds, before the smell hit me, i felt something that wasnt fear. it was closer to pride. like id been right about a friend.

i went back and checked my last nine entries. i wrote "the subject" for the first six. i wrote "Him," capitalized, without meaning to, for the last three. im not a religious person. i dont know what to do with that so, per usual, im just leaving it here and moving on.

unrelated, there was a grey cat that used to sit on the stairwell landing outside my unit and id feed it most nights. i havent been home at a normal hour in six weeks and its not there anymore. thats not a metaphor, im not making it one, i just noticed it tonight and it hit harder than it should have.

— relay

tagged: me · not sleeping 8 comments

the file

every scene, in the order i found them, plus everything i pulled off a dead man's terminal. corrections left in, strikethrough and all.

field notes

in the order i found them. some of these ive gone back and corrected. i left the corrections in, strikethrough and all. felt dishonest to just quietly fix them.

riverfront // mid-level exec residencewk 1

three bodies. one of them was still smoking when i got there, which the coroner's report does not mention, and i am choosing to believe that means something. entry wounds dont match anything standard. more like the round did the damage on the way past, not on impact. no forced entry. building cams glitched for the exact window it happened in. a survivor two doors down says she heard nothing. not muffled. nothing.

working theory: incendiary rounds, custom load.

current theory: something about the weapon burns whoever it kills. not the round. the kill itself.

attached: coroner exchangeclick

asked the coroner's tech why the burn report didnt mention active smoke on arrival. she said scenes dont usually still have smoke by the time she gets the call, and that whoever tagged this one in must have been standing over the body inside a couple minutes of the kill. i didnt tell her that meant i was closer to him than i thought.

logistics yard // off kabukiwk 3

im not going to describe this one in full because i dont think i can and stay professional about it. the room didnt read as a room until the property listing confirmed the square footage. i showed the ballistics tech the photos and he laughed. actually laughed. said nothing does that. i asked what he meant. he said i was asking the wrong question and wouldnt say anything else.

midtown // corpo security detailwk 5

victim found with his own weapon in his mouth. no struggle. no forced entry. footage shows him alone in the room for four minutes before it happened. alone. not even someone in the hallway. NCPD closed it as a psych episode.

i dont think it was.

same block // two days laterwk 6

two of the dead guy's crew killed each other. gun residue on both of them, nothing that doesnt belong to them anywhere in the room. theres no box on an incident report for "weapon used" when the only weapons fired belonged to the victims.

watson // gang holdoutwk 8

she told me she tried to call it in and her own earpiece screamed static back at her before the line even connected. by the time it cleared, it was already over.

third scene where somebody's own comm turned on them for a few seconds right when it mattered. i used to write that off as coincidence. im done writing it off.

pacifica // abandoned towerwk 9

three witnesses, same room, three different descriptions. two of them insist there was a second man they never got a clean look at. the third swears there was nobody else there at all, that the guy just went down on his own.

i believe all three of them. thats the part that worries me.

corpo plaza // stakeout, first one i tried on purposewk 11

sat on a roof access three buildings over for six hours with a directional mic and a very bad feeling. nothing happened, which somehow scared me more than a scene would have. i dont think you stake this out. i think it decides when youre in the room.

i keep the recorder running even when im not on a job now. i dont love what that says about me.

north side // cargo elevator, cross-referencedwk 12

went back to this one myself once i had a code to work off of. corp report says the brake cable failed. i got fifteen minutes alone with the maintenance log before a guard walked me out. the cable didnt fail. it was cut, clean, at an angle no standard maintenance tool in that building makes. adding this to the arsenal file as a fifth signature. i dont love how casually im typing that sentence either.

edit wk 16: went back to this room with a torch four weeks after the fact and found nine casings nobody had bothered to sweep. this is the scene that broke the whole thing open. see ballistics.
service road hideout // tyger clawwk 16 · 28+ dead, 1 alive

the big one. i didnt shoot this scene, it was eleven weeks before i found out about it, i reconstructed it off ncpd photos i paid for and one interview.

the count is between twenty eight and thirty one and nobody has been told which. one of them was called elías. his sister typed his name on this website in wk 23 and it is the only place it is written down. i wrote that as a discrepancy once, the way you write a measurement. someone whose brother is inside the gap between those two numbers read it that way and told me so. rewording it here permanently. every floor of a three storey building and a yard.

what i can read off the photos: he came in the ground floor service entrance, which is the hard way and the loud way and means he wasnt interested in doing it quietly. floors two and three both have bodies stacked toward the stairwell, which means people were running up and away and he was following at a pace where running didnt help. the yard has four out by the fence line. they got furthest. they still didnt get out.

casings on all three floors. all etched. two calibers, which means he swapped weapons mid-building rather than reloading, and swapped back.

one living. see the witnesses section. i cannot stop thinking about the fact that the survivor was on the ground floor, which means he was there in the first minute, and was left alive through the entire rest of it.

✕sponsored
SINGLE RIPPERS
IN YOUR DISTRICT
they are waiting. they have a chair. they are waiting in the chair.
VIEW 47 NEARBY
practitioners are not vetted. district may be approximate. chair may be approximate.
scav den // northside, under the overpasswk 15

organ harvesters. i have shot four scav dens in my career and this is the only one where i had a physical reaction to the room and it wasnt because of what he did to them.

the coolers were untouched. six of them, running, full, and every one still sealed and powered. i checked the seals myself. i checked them twice because i didnt believe it the first time.

whatever happened in that room went around the coolers. not through them. theres a whole approach vector he clearly didnt take, straight through the middle, because the middle is where the coolers are.

NCPD logged the recovery. those went back to families. i went and confirmed that with an intake clerk and then sat in my car for twenty minutes.

ive written fifteen weeks about a man i couldnt find a motive for. this is the first scene ive stood in that had one in it.

6th street warehouse // vista del rey edgewk 16 · zero dead

logging this because it breaks the pattern and i said id log everything, including the parts that dont fit the story im telling.

nine men, a cargo container, a shipment. everyone alive. everyone unconscious. every weapon in the building disabled, and i mean disabled properly, actions removed and taken away, not just magazines dumped.

the container was open and empty. whatever the job was, the job was the container.

not a single casing on the floor. i crawled the whole thing with a torch. he did this one without firing, and given what i now know about how he marks his rounds, i think theres a version of that decision where he simply didnt want his name in a room he wasnt going to fill.

one of the nine talked to me for ten minutes and the only useful thing he said was that the lights went out in a specific order, back to front, and by the time they got to him he had already decided not to reach for anything.

ripperdoc back room // kabukiwk 16

unlicensed cutter working out of a laundromat back room. i know the place. ive been in that chair.

hes not dead. hes not anything, hes just gone, and his gear is gone with him, and the room was cleaned out in a way that reads deliberate rather than panicked.

i want to be careful here because i have an obvious personal stake and im aware of it. the man who put budget optics in my head and sold me a burnt out reflex booster is missing, three days after i posted an entry describing exactly that.

i have no evidence connecting those two things. i have a timeline and a bad feeling and im putting both on the site because thats the deal i made with this thing.

recovered // scene 03 effects

the guy from the midtown scene, wk 5. before he was a case number he had a name and a work terminal that didnt get flagged for corp remote wipe in time. i am not proud of how i got hold of it. im not going to explain how, either. 0dB knows. thats all im saying.

the work

how i get in, how fast, and everything i carry while doing it.

the work

people ask how i get in. this is how. im putting it up because im tired of the dms and because if something happens to me i want somebody to know what my nights actually looked like.

the windowwk 6 · 03:55

whole job lives inside one number. dispatch takes a call, a unit gets assigned, and depending on district that unit takes anywhere from six to nineteen minutes to physically arrive. watson at 3am is nine on a good night. thats my window. i am not brave, i am not stealthy, i am early. thats the entire trick and anyone selling you more than that is selling you something.

i do not enter scenes where anything is still happening. i want that on record. twice ive rolled up and heard something inside and both times i sat in the car and shook and then drove home, and both times i hated myself the whole way. thats the line. its a coward's line and its the only reason im still typing.

one scene, start to finishwk 11 · 04:40

north side. writing it minute by minute because someone asked what its actually like and "you go in and take pictures" isnt an answer.

  • 02:14scanner picks up a shots-fired on a channel i shouldnt have. im already dressed. i sleep dressed now, which is its own entry.
  • 02:16rolling. i dont speed. a stop costs me the entire window and a stop puts my plate in a log on a night i was near a body.
  • 02:23park two blocks out, always uphill, always facing the exit. walk the rest.
  • 02:25boot covers on before i touch the door. gloves. hood up. im not worried about ncpd forensics, theyre worried about closing the ticket. im worried about leaving something a fixer could sell.
  • 02:26inside. i give myself four minutes and i set an actual timer, because ive learned the hard way what a room like that does to your sense of time. you think youve been in there ninety seconds. its been six minutes.
  • 02:26–02:30wide first, always. corners, then the ceiling, then whatevers on the floor, then the thing everyone came for last. shoot the room, not the body. the body is the least useful thing in there and its the only thing amateurs shoot.
  • 02:29the speakers were on. i stood there for eleven seconds of my four minutes just listening. im not going to pretend that was professional.
  • 02:30out. i do not look back at the room from the doorway. thats a habit i built on purpose after the kabuki one.
  • 02:34in the car, doors locked, dumping cards onto two separate shards before i drive anywhere. if im ever stopped leaving a scene i want the copy that matters somewhere that isnt on me.
  • 02:41first unit rolls past me going the other way while im sitting at a light. window was nine minutes. i had fifteen. that means dispatch sat on it, which means somebody wanted it cold before anyone got there, which is a whole other thing i havent figured out yet.
edit: three people have now asked me for the scanner descramble. no. not because im precious about it, because two of you have posted in this guestbook about wanting to "see one in person" and thats not what this is. go outside.

what i actually look for nowwk 12 · 01:20

first two months i shot bodies because thats what sells. now i shoot five things and the body is fifth.

  • 1speakers. always. is it on, what is it, was it on before or after. this is the whole file now.
  • 2the walls behind where people were standing, not the walls behind him. ricochet geometry only reads backwards.
  • 3doors. every single one. which are locked, which are broken, which are untouched. untouched is the interesting one.
  • 4the floor between the door and the far wall, for how fast something crossed it. you can read pace off a room if you know what youre looking at. i didnt three months ago.
  • 5the body. because thats what pays rent.

my kit

everything i carry, what it cost, what its actually for. half of this is held together with tape and i mean that in the boring literal way.

◎
the body — secondhand low-light stills rig, 2071 chassis
the whole business. bought it used with a cracked mount and machined the mount myself out of a shelf bracket because the replacement part costs more than the camera. shoots clean at almost no light, which is the only spec that matters in a room with no working fixtures. i have never once needed a flash and a flash is how you get seen.
▤
the scanner — ncpd band, descrambled
not mine originally, not going to say more than that. this is the single piece of gear the entire operation runs on. everything else is optional. this isnt.
◈
braindance recorder — cheap, consumer grade, barely works
i can record. i cannot properly scrub, layer, or pull secondary sensory tracks, because that is an actual trade and im an actual photographer. i have eleven minutes of BD off the pacifica scene that i am certain has something in it and i have gotten exactly nowhere with it in five weeks. asked around what a real tech charges to edit down a scene. laughed out loud in the guy's shop.
⌁
directional mic + parabolic dish — built it
salvaged driver, a dish off a dead sat unit, foam from a shipping crate. cost me maybe forty eddies in parts. this is what got me the forty minutes of the signal from the vent, so as far as im concerned its the best purchase decision of my life.
▭
two shard readers, one personal link
one reader stays in the car and never comes inside. redundancy isnt paranoia when the whole product is data. link is for pulling off dead terminals, which i can do about as well as any person who watched a tutorial, which is to say badly and slowly.
▣
go-bag
boot covers, gloves, spare cards, a folding step, cash in three denominations, and a printed street map because a printed map cant be pinged. yes i know how that sounds.
👁
optics — budget kiroshi, secondhand, installed wk 8
first chrome ive put in my head in nine years. bottom tier, refurbished, from a guy operating out of a laundromat back room. i told myself it was a work expense, better low light, better zoom, ranging. and it is. thats all true.
its also the exact category of thing he has, which is not why i bought them, and which i thought about every day for a week after.
⬢
the car — 2047 shitbox, four hundred eddies and a favor
destroyed wk 15. replaced wk 15, eleven minutes later, by the subject of this website, with a bow on it.
i have not driven it since the day i got it home. it sits outside my building and i look at it out the window and every person on my block has now seen a man like me get out of a car like that. i used to work by being early and unremarkable. i cannot be unremarkable in that car. the gift took the only real skill i had.
i also cant sell it, obviously. its in my name. thats the joke. thats the whole joke.
✕
[ not installed ]
bought a reflex booster off the same laundromat guy in wk 13. burnt out unit, previous owner unknown, no paperwork, and he was very clear that a proper ripper wouldnt touch it.
its been in my cold box for eleven days. i take it out and look at it and put it back. i know exactly what it is. its me trying to buy a half second so i can be in a room at the speed hes in a room, and there is no version of that sentence where im the reasonable one.
regina has seventeen files. she showed me. i keep thinking about how every single one of those seventeen bought their first piece for a reason that sounded practical out loud.
im not going to install it. writing that here so its written down somewhere i cant quietly take it back.
addendum wk 15: he has read this page. he has read this specific entry. he knew what was in my cold box and what i bought it for and he did not say one word about it, and then he solved the exact problem i bought it to solve by handing me a faster car instead.
i threw it in the incinerator chute on the tuesday. not because i got wise. because i couldnt stand him having read about it.

the subject

chrome, wounds, and brass. everything i have managed to work out about what he is running and what it does to a room.

the chrome

what ive pieced together about what hes running. take it with salt. ive been wrong about most of this at least once already.

the eyes

every scene, he already seems to know the room before hes fully in it. cover, exits, who's carrying. one witness swore his eyes glow, actual glow, not a trick of bad light. i didnt believe her until a second witness said the same thing without me asking.

the arms

this is the one that broke my working theory more than once.

  • discardedtwo men, unrelated, coincidence of method.
  • discardedcybernetic malfunction causing inconsistent witness recall.
  • currenthe changes his own rig between jobs. blade work on some scenes, bare-handed blunt trauma on others. doesnt want a signature.

he has one. he just doesnt know it yet.

speed / not there

more than one witness describes the room slowing down around him, or him just not being where he should be a half second later. a guy at the pacifica scene swears the man standing in front of him blinked out mid-sentence and didnt come back until it was already over. i used to file that under adrenaline and bad memory. i dont anymore.

some nights i catch myself hoping the room slows down for me too, if it ever comes to that. i dont know why i wrote that sentence. im leaving it, same as everything else.

working it out from the roomswk 16 · 02:30

ive stopped asking witnesses what they saw. witnesses give you adjectives. rooms give you numbers. everything below came off physical evidence or footage, not off a person's memory, and its the first version of this file i'd defend to somebody hostile.

the slow
its real and its measurable.
pulled two building cams. both have him entering frame and then a gap where the timestamp keeps counting and he simply relocates between frames, further than a person covers in that interval. its not dropped frames, the counter is continuous and everyone else in shot moves normally across the same window. either the footage is being altered in a way that leaves the timestamp intact, or he crossed eleven meters inside a fifth of a second. i have stopped assuming its the first one.
the armour
people hit him. it does not matter.
this is the find im proudest of. six deformed slugs across three scenes, flattened, recovered off floors well inside the room, at angles that put the impact surface at roughly chest height on a standing man. flattened means they hit something that did not give.

no blood with any of them. not a drop, not on the slug, not under where it landed. hes been shot at least six times that i can prove and there is no physical evidence he was injured on any occasion.
the gone
he leaves rooms he is provably still in.
two separate scenes have a survivor or a cam showing him break contact in an enclosed space with one exit that he did not use. kabuki has him in a corridor and then not in a corridor. its consistent enough that im comfortable saying he can stop being visible on demand and that the effect is short, because both times it happens immediately before he does something.
the ones with no shooter
a whole category of death where he was never in the room.
midtown, week 5. the pair two days later. at least three more since. weapon discharged, residue on the victim's own hands, no second party on any footage, no forced entry. i logged these separately for months because they didnt look like his work. they are. its the same nights, the same buildings, the same station playing after.

what that means is that some unknown fraction of this file is deaths he caused from outside the building. i have no way to know how large that fraction is and it makes every number on this site a floor rather than a total.
the comms
people cant call for help and cant hear each other.
five accounts now of an earpiece screaming static at the exact moment it mattered, or of shouting to somebody twelve feet away and getting nothing back. its not jamming, jamming would take the whole block out and it doesnt. its selective and its per-person.
the seeing
he knows the room before he is in it.
nobody clears corners. no check patterns, no pausing at thresholds, no doubling back. in every reconstruction i have he moves through a building on a route that only makes sense if he already knew where every person in it was standing. and the eyes. the eyes come up in every account i have and i have stopped treating that as folklore.
the coming back
two people have described him going down and getting up.
im flagging this as unverified because both are secondhand and both were hysterical. but they are separated by six weeks, they dont know each other, and they used almost the same phrasing. if its real then the last hard limit i had on this file is gone, because everything else on this list is expensive and this one would just be unfair.

i want to put the total somewhere in plain words.

hes faster than the room. hes armoured past the point where being shot is an event. he can stop being visible. he can kill people in buildings he is not inside. he can take away your ability to call for help and your ability to hear the person next to you. he sees everyone before they see him. and he might not stay down.

and hes carrying all of it at once, coherent, on a schedule, with a sense of humour about it.

regina told me she has seventeen files of people who crossed the line and lost themselves. i understood what she meant at the time. i understand it differently now, which is that everything on that list above is a thing a person buys, and a person who has bought all of it has spent a fortune and a great deal of their own body on the ability to be in a room the way he is in a room.

nobody spends that much to be that thorough about it unless being thorough is the point.

ballistics

the entry where i explain that ive been a bad investigator for fifteen weeks. put a bucket next to you.

i finally picked one upwk 16 · 03:12

somebody in the comments, and im not going to say who because theyve asked me not to, sent me a message that just said "youve photographed 400 casings. how many have you held."

none. the answer was none.

i shoot the room. thats my whole method, its in the work section, im very proud of it. wide first, corners, ceiling, floor, body last. i have photographed the floor of every scene ive ever been to and casings are part of the floor and the floor is a texture, and thats how i had been thinking about it. as texture.

went back to the north side elevator scene at 2am with a torch. its four weeks cold, nobodys cleaned it because nobody cleans anything out there. found nine.

theyre etched.

every one. and not scratched, not stamped, not hand-scribed by a guy with a pick. machined. even depth, even kerning, wraps the case perfectly so the last character meets the first with no gap. i have shot product stills for jewelers who charge four figures and their work is not this clean.

PROPERTY OF V

on all nine.

then i went back through my archive. every scene, four months, full res, zoomed all the way in on the floor.

its on all of them. every casing at every scene since week one.

it was on the floor of the first room i ever walked into.

i paid a man in dogtown a serious amount of money for a photograph of a licence plate with one letter on it. i wrote four thousand words theorizing about what the letter stood for. i ruled out that it was a name because i decided nobodys name is one letter.

the answer has been lying on the ground, in machined capitals, in every room, the entire time. i stood in those rooms. i walked on it.

tagged: ballistics · things i got wrong · the letter 96 comments
the casings, to scalewk 16 · 04:40

a reader offered to teach me enough to build this. four nights of him being patient with me over voice while i broke it repeatedly. its not good code. it spins. thats all i wanted it to do.

three casings i have physically recovered, modelled to size off calipers, with the etching where the etching actually sits. drag to turn them.

drag to spin

thats the part that gets me. look at the small one. thats a submachine gun round, it is smaller than the last joint of my little finger, and he had it engraved. he engraves the ammunition he sprays ninety rounds a minute of. into walls. on purpose, off walls, so they bounce.

the big one is a different problem. i cant find a production weapon that chambers it. its an absurd round. whatever fires that was not made for a person to carry comfortably and he carries it anyway.

what the casings actually tell mewk 16 · 05:25
finding 01
the etching is pre-firing.
deformation from the extractor runs over the top of the letters, not under. so theyre cut into brass before he ever loads them. this isnt something done to a scene afterwards. he prepares this at home, in advance, in bulk, for rounds he has not yet decided who to use on.
finding 02
nobody makes these.
no manufacturer stamp, no lot code, no headstamp of any kind on any of the three. commercial ammunition is legally required to carry both. these are handloaded or custom ordered in a quantity that makes custom ordering absurd, and either answer costs more per round than most people in this city make in an hour.
finding 03
its the same hand across every caliber.
same typeface, same relative letter height, same spacing logic scaled to the case. a shotgun shell and a smg round are wildly different surfaces and the work reads identically on both. one process. one person's standard.
finding 04
he does not pick them up.
a man who signs his ammunition and then leaves it on the floor is not signing it for himself. and hes not doing it for the cops, ncpd bagged casings from at least four of these scenes and closed all four anyway. so its for whoever comes looking. it is a signature left for a reader who does not exist yet.
finding 05
the cost of it.
i costed the machining time. even at bulk, even with a good setup, engraving to that tolerance is minutes per round. he fired ninety of them into one room in kabuki. thats an afternoon of work, spent, so that a room he was going to leave anyway would have his name on the floor of it.

so heres my read, and its the first one in a while i actually feel steady about.

this is the same behaviour as the station. the same as sourcing a 1988 demo when a cleaner version exists. the same as getting all seven tracks. its a person who does the unnecessary, complete, expensive version of a thing because the incomplete version would bother him. the etching isnt a threat and its not theatre for an audience, because for fifteen weeks there was no audience, i was standing on it and not looking down.

he does it because he'd know it wasnt done.

edit: yes i have considered that he started etching them because of this site. no. i pulled week one full res. its on the week one casings. i had it before i had anything.

the one he leftwk 16 · 23:10

this is the best witness i have ever had and hes almost useless and i have been sitting on this interview for four days trying to work out how to write it up.

tyger claw. low level, runner, not muscle. twenty two. hideout off a service road, and by every count i can get, either twenty eight or thirty one people in the building that night.

one came out.

hes not in hiding. thats the first thing that threw me. his own people wont go near him now, which he seems to understand and accept, and he agreed to talk to me in a noodle place in daylight with his back to the door. he has a plate in his jaw and hes missing chrome out of both arms that he says was taken out of him rather than damaged, which i dont fully understand and neither does he.

q: can you walk me through it
no. not the middle part. i can do the start and i can do the end.
q: the end then
im on the floor. i cant get up, both arms are done. and he comes over and he crouches down. not standing over me. crouches. puts his weight on me, on my chest, one knee, like youd hold something down thats gonna wriggle.
q: and then
he takes my face and turns it so im looking at him. and he waits.
q: waits for what
for me to look at him. properly. i kept trying to look off and he'd just turn my head back. patient about it. like a guy fixing a picture on a wall thats not level.
q: what did he say
nothing.
q: nothing at the time, or nothing you remember
nothing. not one word. not a sound. thats the thing im telling you, choom, thats the actual thing. i have been over it every night for eleven weeks. he did not say anything.
q: what did you see
red. and i know thats what everybody says, i know how that sounds. but its not glowing red like people say, its behind, its underneath the eye. and hes looking at you the way you look at something youre making sure youve properly seen.
q: and then he left
he got up and he walked out. thats it. he didnt look back at me from the door. i want to be clear that i thought i was dead for about a minute after, i just laid there waiting for it and it didnt come.

then he said the thing thats been in my head since and its the reason ive taken four days.

"everyone keeps asking me what the message was. what was he telling you, what did he want you to pass on. there wasnt one. i keep trying to make there be one because if theres a message then i got picked for a reason and i can do something with it. there isnt. he didnt want me to tell anybody anything. he wanted me to have seen him. thats all it was. i was there so it got seen."

and i sat in that noodle place and i understood, about four seconds too late to keep my face straight, that i have just been given the exact same treatment through a slower medium.

he took my site down and he put it back up. he emptied a club and put my music on and put four words on every screen in it. he blew up my car and gave me another one with a bow on it and dropped the keys on my head. no explanation. no demand. no message. nothing i can act on and nothing i can pass on.

he did to me what he did to this kid.
he just used a website instead of his hands.

i asked him at the end if he was okay. stupid question, i know. he said hes going to a ripper next month to have the empty sockets in his arms closed up and hes not replacing the chrome, and when i asked why not he shrugged and said hes not interested in it anymore.

i wrote him down as the luckiest man in night city in my notes on the drive over. i crossed it out in the parking lot after.

kabuki, 04:10, parkedwk 14

this is the closest ive been and i want to write it carefully because ive already caught myself embellishing it twice when telling people out loud.

it was parked. not moving, not fleeing, parked, on a street with three working cameras and a noodle stand still open. i was on foot, half a block up. i stood there for a minute and forty seconds and did not raise my camera.

i have thought about that minute forty every day since. i had the shot. it was the shot. four months of work and a clean plate photo at eleven meters and i stood there with my hands at my sides like a tourist.

i told myself afterwards it was tactical. it wasnt. the truth is i didnt want to be the guy who took it. i dont fully understand that sentence yet and im not going to pretend to.

edit: the noodle stand was open, which means the owner was there, which means there is a person in this city who served food forty meters from that car and thought nothing of it. i went back three nights running to ask her. she wont talk to me. i think shes made me as someone whos going to make her night worse.

the thing about the plate lightwk 14

three separate sightings, three separate people, and all three mention there was no light on the plate. i assumed that was him hiding it. stood in front of it myself now and thats not what it is.

theres no light because the plate isnt registered to a system that requires one. its not concealment. its that the rules the light exists to satisfy dont apply to whatever that plate is.

the signal

the only thing i have that is actually his.

the signal

the only thing i have thats actually his.

everything else in this file could belong to a lot of people. chrome gets swapped. guns get replaced or scrapped down for parts. this one thing hasnt changed across four separate scenes, and its the reason i started thinking of this as one person instead of a rumor with good PR.

after its over, if the location has a working comm or speaker system, it plays. not static, not a jam signal. a station. it doesnt show up on any registered frequency list ive been able to pull, public or gray market. i sat in a vent above one scene for forty minutes with a recorder just to log what i could.

what the dating actually meanswk 13 · 02:08

i sat down to date the tracklist expecting nothing and it turned into the most useful night of work ive done on this whole file. heres the finding, and its bigger than it looks.

none of this is on any service. not a paid one, not a gray one, not a corp archive. the labels are gone. most of these acts were on labels that died before the unification war and never got digitized by anyone with rights to do it. a good half of it never had a rights holder to begin with. you cannot stream this. there is no place to click.

which means somebody physically sourced all of it. disc by disc, rip by rip, off dead formats, out of collections, from people who kept boxes in closets through two wars. thats not a playlist. thats an archive. thats years.

and heres the part i keep chewing on. the deep cuts arent the album versions. hes got the 1988 demo of a track that has a cleaner 1991 release. hes got a live recording from one specific night in sydney. hes got a demo version of a 2007 track instead of the actual record. you do not end up with those by accident, you end up with those because you went looking specifically, past the easy version, for the one that is harder to find.

i have spent four months building a picture of a man from wounds and burn patterns and none of it told me anything a hundred other people in this city couldnt also do. this tells me he is patient. it tells me he is a completionist. it tells me when he finds something he likes he does not stop at the surface, he goes and gets all seven tracks, and he keeps them, and he plays them for an empty room after.

thats not a monster's hobby. thats just a guy's hobby. i think thats why this one rattled me more than the crime scenes did.

edit: someone in the comments asked why i think its him curating and not a jammed feed hes piggybacking. because a jammed feed repeats on a loop and this doesnt. forty minutes, no repeats, and the sequencing is deliberate. it goes from a 2008 rap track into a 200 year old requiem about judgment day and back out into something recorded in a garage. somebody built that order. somebody thought about that order.

the sevenwk 13 · 23:30

one act shows up seven times. nothing else on the station gets more than two. no release dates i can find, no label, no distribution, nothing in any index. that combination should mean it doesnt exist, and it obviously does, because i have forty minutes of it on a shard.

which points at physical media. bootlegs, hand-dubbed, sold at shows or out of a box. that is a small world. that is people who know each other. that is, for the first time in four months, an actual door.

found a dealer who moves that kind of thing. burned my last real favor getting an introduction. hes agreed to meet me and hes already told me twice that he wont answer questions about buyers.

i dont care. if the guy im chasing bought seven tracks off somebody, then somebody has met him, and has sold him something, and stood across a table from him while he decided what he wanted. thats closer than a burn pattern ever got me.

wk 53 — two additions

the station changed. first time in a year it has changed. two tracks that were not there before, and one of them undoes a thing i wrote three weeks ago.

i noticed because i had the listwk 53

ive had the dish out most nights since the hundred and three, on the theory that if it ever happens again i would like to be recording before it starts rather than after.

nothing has happened again. the city has been quieter for a month than i have ever known it.

but the station still runs, and i still capture it when i can find it, and last week two things came through that are not on my week seventeen list. i built that list over nineteen hours and i know it better than i know most people.

and heres the thing i want at the top, before either of them, because it is bigger than both and everybody is going to scroll past it to get to the songs.

nothing has been added to that station
in the entire time i have been listening.

fifty three weeks. i have captured that band on and off since week eight and properly since week seventeen, and i have never once heard anything on it that was not on the list i built in november.

not after the club. not after the arm. not after the wall, or the money, or the sixteen days, or the hundred and three. a man who reconstructed a computer chassis to match a dent, who bought a whole catalogue at full asking for six years, who put a functioning braindance together for a prank — has not added one track to his own radio station in a year.

thats not neglect. hes clearly still building things. its a standard.

the set is closed. it has been closed the entire time i have known about it, and i wrote nineteen hours of analysis on the assumption that it was a finished object, and it turns out i was right and i did not understand what that meant.

and then two in one week.

both captures below. theyre off a homemade parabolic through a wall, so they sound like what they are.

soulja boy tell'em. c. 2007. and its the uncensored version, which is the part that matters — the one that was never on a release, never on a service, and only ever existed as a raw upload on two platforms that both died before the unification war.

tape_hiss has already been at me about this one and hes right and ill let him say it in the comments.

the short version: this is the internet wing again. this is a file that was on a video site and a filesharing network seventy years ago and nowhere else, ever, in any commercial form. there is no rights holder. there is no master. there is no clean copy anywhere in existence because a clean copy was never made.

what he has is somebody's rip. and the rip is bad, and it was bad when it was made, and it has been carried across seventy years of format changes by people who thought it was worth carrying and it still sounds like that.

i wrote in week seventeen that the internet block was the part that genuinely frightened me. label releases survive because objects survive. this doesnt survive. somebody kept it, deliberately, personally, one file at a time.

its custody. tape_hiss said that in week seventeen and i have never found a better word.

and then i sat down very slowlywk 53 · 02:40

the courier. site 03. three weeks ago.

he was covered head to boots and he could not stand still and he talked at me for nineteen minutes and the thing he opened with, the thing he came back to eleven times, the thing i transcribed exactly as he said it including the volume because taking the volume out would have been dishonest —

"HE CAME IN HERE LIKE —
YAAAHHH!!!!!!!"

i logged that as a sound effect. i wrote in the entry that he does the sound effects with his whole body. everybody in the comments read it as a battle cry. thirty thousand people quoted it. somebody put it on a shirt.

its a song title.

i cannot establish which way round it goes and i want to be honest that i have tried for two days. either the track was playing and the courier heard it and reproduced it back at me without knowing what it was, or the man came through a door at half three in the morning doing a seventy year old ad-lib out loud because it was in his head.

and i genuinely cannot tell you which of those is more likely, because i have eleven months of evidence for both, and because the second one is exactly the sort of thing he does and the first one is exactly the sort of thing he does.

what i can tell you is that i had the answer in my own transcript for three weeks and it took a track appearing on a radio station for me to see it.

the courier has read this. he messaged me within about an hour of it going up. he said, and im quoting with permission, "so hes just a guy who likes a song." he has not been alright for three weeks and i think that sentence did more for him than anything ive been able to say to him.

what nineteen hours got mewk 17 +5 · 02:40
finding 01
he collects people, not bands.
one performer appears four or five times across forty years under four different act names in three different genres. that is not somebody with a taste in music. that is somebody who found a person interesting and then went and got everything.
finding 02
he plays whole records.
album intros. outro freestyles. seven tracks of one release in sequence. i catalogued individual songs for two months because i was listening like a man with a playlist, and he has never once been doing a playlist.
finding 03
every single time there are two versions, he has the worse-sounding one.
the 1989 cassette demo over the 1991 studio album. the 2007 demo over the release. the live sydney take over the record. the original title over the edit. its consistent to the point of being a rule, and the rule is not "better quality," the rule is closer to the source.
finding 04
half of this cannot exist.
the internet wing is the part that genuinely frightens me now. label releases survive because objects survive. the breakcore, the mashcore, the jerk tracks, the file with .mp3 in its own title — those were uploaded by individuals to services that have been dead for fifty years. there is no institution anywhere that preserved them. somebody did, personally, one file at a time, and then carried them forward through every format change since.
finding 05
six years, minimum. probably far longer.
the dealer says somebody has bought every release by one of these acts for six years without haggling once. thats one act. there are thirty on this station. if that behaviour is consistent across all of them then the station isnt a collection he assembled, its a collection he has been maintaining for most of his adult life.

and the thing i keep arriving at, which i did not expect to arrive at:

this is the only part of him that isnt about anybody else. the chrome is for work. the guns are for work. the etching is for whoever comes looking. the car gets him places. every single thing i have catalogued about this man in four months is instrumental, its all for something.

this isnt. nobody was listening to that station. for years nobody was listening to that station. he built it, and he maintained it, and he put it on the speakers of rooms after everyone in them was dead, for an audience of one.

its the only hobby he has. i went looking for a weakness for four months and what i actually found is that hes a guy who likes music a lot.

the huey lewis track, solvedwk 17 +5 · 14:20

somebody in the guestbook took about four minutes to work out what i could not do in nineteen hours, and the answer reframes the whole station.

its not a music release. its audio ripped out of a film.

a film from 2000, about a man who murders people and cannot get anyone to notice, and the scene the audio comes from is the one where he plays that specific song to a colleague, delivers a long sincere monologue about how good the band is, and then kills him with an axe while it plays.

the minute of talking is the monologue. the passage i identified as a person being killed is a person being killed.

and heres the part that makes it a finding rather than a curiosity. that song was on the film's soundtrack album for about a week before it was pulled, and something like a hundred thousand copies were recalled. so the "american psycho version" is not a thing you can buy. it has never been a thing you can buy. the only way to have it is to own the film and take the audio out yourself.

so he has the film. he watched the film. he liked a scene enough to extract ninety seconds of it, and then he put it on a station he plays in rooms after he has finished working.

ive spent four months building a profile out of wound geometry and machining tolerances. this is the first thing in the entire file that tells me what he thinks is funny, and its the blackest joke available and he has been telling it, to nobody, for years.

i have also now watched the film. it took me a day to find a copy. i understand the joke completely and i am not going to explain it any further than i already have, partly because it would take a long time and partly because i now feel implicated in a way i cant articulate.

six fixers, one bar, and one character on a licence plate.

the letter

wk 13–14. the longest thing ive written and the least ive ever known at the end of writing something. sorry in advance.

NOTE BEFORE YOU READ: i spent most of two months savings on this and i want to be honest that i knew it was a bad financial decision while i was making it. im behind on rent. im telling you that because if i leave it out this reads like a man in control of himself.
i asked six fixers about himwk 13 · 04:12

this is the part where i stopped being a guy with a camera and started being a guy asking questions in rooms where questions cost money. i dont recommend it. heres all six, in the order i got to them.

WAKAKO OKADA — japantown, the pachinko parlor on jig-jignothing

she poured me tea. she asked about my mother, who ive never mentioned to anyone in this city. she answered zero of my questions and she did it so pleasantly that i was halfway to my car before i realized id been handled.

one thing. when i said what i was working on, she stopped pouring. just for a second. then she kept pouring. thats the whole interview and i still think about that second.

EL CAPITÁN — rancho coronado, santo domingobrief

ex corpo, doesnt hide it, doesnt like being asked about it either. gave me maybe ninety seconds.

"you want my professional opinion? there is no man. there is a hole in the market and something moving through it very fast. you are asking me to describe the shape of a thing by describing the hole. i have work to do."

then he told me to eat something. i must have looked worse than i thought.

DAKOTA SMITH — badlandsthe car

oldest fixer out past the wall, nomad, keeps an oxygen line on her the whole time she talks to you. didnt charge me. said she doesnt charge people who look like i looked.

"passed me on the long stretch doing something a car that size should not be able to do. black. no plate light. thing is, i didnt hear it coming. out there you hear everything for a mile. i heard it leaving. thats it. thats what ive got and its been eating at me since."

PADRE — vista del rey, heywoodthe one that stuck

sebastian ibarra. was a priest with the valentinos before moto cielo, does fixer work now, still talks like a man who never fully put the collar down. i went in expecting a runaround. i got the closest thing to a straight answer anyone gave me and i wish i hadnt.

"i have buried men who believed they were owed a reckoning, mijo. they arrive loud. they want it witnessed. this one does not ask to be owed anything. he arrives, the debt is settled, he leaves before anyone thinks to be afraid of him. that is not a man working."

i asked him what it is, then.

"weather. you do not investigate weather. you go inside, you close the shutters, and you thank god it passed over your house and not through it. go home. call your family. you have that look about you that the ones who dont call have."

i called my sister that night for the first time since february. we talked for eleven minutes about nothing. i dont know why im putting that on a website.

REGINA JONES — yaiba tower, kabukiread this one

ex media. world news service, then FTF radio until a conglomerate ate it. shes been a fixer for years now but she still talks like a reporter, and shes the only person i spoke to who was already keeping her own file on him. she pulled it up. she let me look at it. i still dont fully understand why.

her interest isnt what i expected. shes not tracking him because hes dangerous. shes tracking him because of what hes carrying.

"i keep records on everyone in this city walking around with more chrome in them than a body is built to tolerate. i have seventeen case files. seventeen people who crossed that line and lost themselves on the other side of it, and i got to most of them after. he is carrying more than any of the seventeen. by a distance. and he is coherent. he is making plans. he is showing up where he means to show up."

i asked if that was good news.

"it is the best news i have ever had or the worst and i have not decided which. either the line is further out than we thought, which changes everything i have worked on for six years. or he crossed it a long time ago and it simply looks like this now. thats the one that keeps me up."

then she looked at my notes. the actual notebook, upside down across her desk, for about four seconds. and then she said the thing im still not over.

"youre doing what i did. eleven years i did that. then one night i understood that the story had started looking back, and i quit and became something that gets to decide who finds it. you dont have that. you have a website. put it down."

i didnt put it down. obviously. youre reading it.

MR. HANDS — dogtownexpensive

took my money before i finished the sentence. gave me one thing back. i want to be clear that one thing was more than everyone else gave me combined and i still feel robbed, which i think is the entire business model.

"for your money: a plate. that is what your money buys. what you do with one letter is entirely your business, and i would encourage you, as someone with no stake in your wellbeing whatsoever, to do nothing with it at all."

the afterlife, and a question i shouldnt have askedwk 13 · 23:58

got in on a referral i burned a real favor for. wont say whose. the bar names drinks after mercs who died in a way the city wants to remember, thats the whole tradition, thats what the place is. i asked the woman behind the bar, russell, ex militech engineer, does the menu, if he had one yet.

"no. cant. rule is you gotta snuff it spectacular, preferably mid op, and he hasnt done us the courtesy yet. people ask though. more of em every month. thats usually how it starts."

so heres what i actually got out of the most expensive night of my life. hes alive. thats it. thats the finding. after four months, the first hard confirmation i have that hes a living person and not a story the city tells itself is that a bartender cant name a drink after him yet.

ive read that back maybe thirty times. its still the most solid thing in the whole file.

one letter. thats what four months and two months rent bought me. i have sat with this for nine days.

heres every direction i took it, in order, so you can watch me do it:

people were already saying it.

i thought i started it. i genuinely thought the plate leaked out of dogtown through me, that i put a letter into circulation and the street picked it up and ran, and some sick little part of me was proud of that. so i went back through my own notes to date the spread.

they were saying it before i ever paid for the plate. the nomad said it in week seven. birdie wrote something on a napkin in week four and burned it and i never asked what the word was, but its four letters shorter than i assumed and i know exactly what it was now.

the plate isnt the source. the plate isnt a clue he dropped. the plate is just his. he put it on his own car. in a city where every single person i talked to who knows anything about him wouldnt say it above a whisper, he printed it and bolted it to the front of a car that cant be repainted and drives at a speed nobody can follow.

which would mean hes never been hiding, and ive spent four months, my savings, and whatever i used to be, running an investigation into a man who has his name on his car.

or hes just a guy named V and im the only person in night city who couldnt hear it.

vista del rey. heywood. which is padres district, and padre is the man who sat across from me and told me to go home, close the shutters and call my family. i drove past his corner on the way. i want to believe thats a coincidence and i am done believing things are coincidences.

the club is valentinos-owned. señor ladrillo's place. big red sign, the animated one, you know the one. its the biggest gay club in the city and on any night of the week theres a line down the block and a cashier taking a hundred eddies a head at the door.

i genuinely do not know how it was done and i want to be straight about that instead of pretending. could have been a quickhack, everything in that car had just enough electronics in it to cook. could have been a round from a roof, and there are three roofs on that street with the angle. i went and looked at all three like a moron, in the daylight, with my ears still ringing.

a caliburn came around the corner

i drove a caliburn back to my apartment in heywood, in the clothes id slept in, with soot on my jacket, doing exactly the speed limit the entire way because i was terrified of being pulled over in a car i could not begin to explain owning.

wk 17 — he was in the room

im posting this five days late. i needed the five days. some of this is going to read badly and i have decided not to fix that.

3:33wk 17 · posted 22:40, five days after

i woke up. not gradually. awake, all at once, flat on my back, eyes open.

3:33
the first thing i looked at

i have gone round and round on this and i want to put the whole loop on the page instead of just the conclusion, because the loop is the actual experience.

  • noa reference. i pulled everything. numerology, scripture, three different gang numerologies, a corp designation, an old emergency code. all of it fits and none of it fits, which is how you know youre doing astrology.
  • noa callback to the station number. i wanted this one badly. 69.420 and 3:33 have nothing to do with each other and i spent two hours making a chart trying.
  • nocoincidence. i wake up at 4:50 for work. ive woken at 3-something maybe twice in a year and both times i had been drinking.
  • unresolvedthat he did it. that theres something that reaches into a man with cheap optics in his head and switches him on at a time of its choosing. i dont know if thats possible. i know he has done four things to me that i also didnt think were possible and i have stopped using that word as evidence.

and the real answer, the one under all of it: i dont know. i will never know. that might be the whole point of picking a time that looks like it means something.

a man who ties a bow onto a car would absolutely pick a stupid clock time on purpose. i keep landing there and i keep hating it.

the smellwk 17

i knew it before i was upright. thats the part i cant explain to anyone who doesnt do what i do.

there is a specific smell to a body and it is not the smell of meat or of a bin or of anything else, and after four months of standing in rooms with it, my body knows it faster than my head does. i have smelled it maybe forty times and every one of those times i was somewhere i had driven to on purpose.

it was in my bedroom.

i lay there for a while before i turned over. im not proud of the number of seconds but it was a lot of them.

the other side of the bedwk 17

i keep a second pillow. theres no one who sleeps on it. its been there since i moved in and ive never once thought about why i still make that side of the bed.

he thought about it. thats where he put it.

a right arm. taken off midway up the humerus.

and its clean. i need you to understand what i mean, because this site has spent four months describing rooms that were reduced to material and this is the opposite of that.

the cut is flat. one pass. bone, muscle, skin, all on the same plane with no lipping, no drag, no stutter, no second attempt. i have photographed surgical amputations for insurance work. a top tier ripper with a proper saw and a clamped limb and no time pressure does not get a face like that. theres no thermal margin either, so it wasnt cauterised, which means it was cut cold and it was cut in one motion and it was cut by something that did not slow down going through the bone.

and there is almost no blood. on the arm, on the pillow, on the sheet, on my floor. he cut it somewhere else and then carried it into my bedroom while i was asleep, and set it down on the side of the bed nobody uses, and left.

what i did next, in order, because it says something about me and i said id be honest on this site: i photographed it. that was first. before the door, before the windows, before checking whether he was still in the apartment. i took forty one frames of a human arm in my own bed and i did it on autopilot and i did not have a feeling about it until i was done.
i knew the tattoowk 17

and then i turned the arm over. and i knew it immediately, and thats when i stopped being a person taking photographs.

i went to school with the man this arm belonged to.

im not going to put his name up. not out of respect. i want to be exact about that, because i think what im about to write is worse if you think im being gracious. im not naming him because ive spent a decade and a half doing the work of not thinking about him and typing it out feels like undoing that.

he made three years of my life a place i had to survive rather than live in. daily. inventive about it. the kind where you learn to plan a route through a building. i have been an adult for a long time now and i had genuinely, actually, mostly forgotten he existed. that was the achievement. that took years.

and heres the part i have been sitting with for five days.

i was glad.

not for long. maybe two seconds. but it was there, it was clean and it was uncomplicated and it arrived before the horror did, and i felt it in a room that had a piece of him in it, and no amount of what came afterwards takes those two seconds back.

hes dead, presumably, or worse than dead, because of a website i made. because i wrote things down. a man i hadnt thought about since before this city was my problem is gone, and the reason is that i got interested in something.

i have not decided if that makes me responsible. ive decided i dont get to be the one who decides.

howwk 17

this is the question that has actually stopped me sleeping, more than the arm did.

that man is not in my life. hes not in my records. we were kids in a different part of the world over twenty years ago, before i was relay, before any of this, under a name i dont use. theres no file that connects us. i have never written about him anywhere. i have never said his name out loud in this city. i checked, obsessively, for two days, whether id ever mentioned it in anything that could be read, and i havent, because you dont mention the thing you spent years not mentioning.

  • noi let it slip somewhere and forgot. i have been through everything. every entry, every message, every interview recording i still have. its not there.
  • openhe went back through twenty year old records under my real name. which he has. which he put on a licence plate. that would take resources and it would take a reason to bother, and the second one is what i cant get past.
  • open, and i hate ithe was there. same years, same age bracket, if hes anywhere near the age people describe. that would mean he already knew, before any of this, without looking anything up.

i have gone through the second one properly. faces, years, everyone i can still picture. i cant place him. i also couldnt pick him out of a room today, which is the entire problem with this file and always has been.

i dont think its true. i think its the worse story and i think im drawn to it because after five days i would genuinely rather this be personal than be a demonstration of how much he can find out about anybody he decides to look at.

thats the honest state of it. i dont know how he knew and i never will, and that is going to be true for the rest of my life.

the hand was closedwk 17

i noticed it late. the fist was balled. tight.

you learn what that means. a hand doesnt end up like that by being carried. thats a hand that was holding something, or was closed around something and then set.

it took me a while to open it. longer than i want to write down.

MORE INFORMATION
WILL COME
AS YOU NEED IT
; )
carved into the palm. not written. not inked.

cut into the skin of the palm. and it is the same standard as the casings. even depth, even spacing, following the curve of the hand without a single hesitation mark or correction. i have seen high end scarification work, ive photographed it for a shop in kabuki. this is better than that. this is better than anything a person should be able to do to a surface that soft.

and then the wink.

i have looked at that for five days. two marks and a bracket, carved, by hand, with the same precision as the rest of it, into a dead man i knew when i was fifteen.

its a joke. it is a joke, the same as the club was a joke, the same as the bow was a joke. hes being playful. hes doing a bit, with me, and hes committed enough to the bit to carve the punctuation.

everyone reading this has spent months wanting to know what he is. hes someone who makes an emoticon out of a body, at a level of craft that took real time, and then goes home.

afterwardswk 17

door was locked, from the inside, chain on. windows shut. building cam covers the stairwell and has forty minutes of nothing in it. no forced entry anywhere and i went over that apartment for six hours.

i cant call it in. obviously i cant call it in. i have an arm and no way to explain owning one, on a night i was home alone, belonging to a man who has a documented reason to have hated me twenty years ago.

im not going to say what i did with it. it is handled and it was not disrespectful and thats all thats going on the site. if that costs me readers, fine.

i sat on my floor afterwards with the sun coming up and worked out that this is the fourth time now. site taken down and put back. the club and the screens. the car. this.

four times, and not one word. everything ive learned about him ive learned from things he has done in front of me and left for me to find. hes never once explained himself and hes never going to.

the kid from the service road said he was there so it got seen. im getting the long version of the same thing. hes not telling me anything. hes showing me, over and over, on a schedule of his choosing, and the only thing i can do about it is keep writing down what i saw.

which is what he wants. which i know. which doesnt change what im going to do tomorrow.

— relay

wk 17, the next night — he was watching the whole time

one day after the arm. im writing this the same night, still up, and im not going to be able to make it orderly so im doing it as it happened.

my machine restartedwk 17 +1 · 21:48

i was editing. mid sentence, on the ballistics post, tidying something nobody would ever have noticed.

screen went. i assumed a crash, thats a nine year old rig, it does that.

HIDE NOW
flashing. nothing else on the screen.

and i want to be honest about my actual first reaction, which was not fear, it was irritation, because i thought it was a joke and i thought i had lost forty minutes of work.

my second reaction was to say out loud, to an empty apartment, "hide where." because you have to understand my place. one room. a bed, a desk, a wardrobe with a broken runner, a kitchen strip, a bathroom you cannot lock. there is nowhere in it. there has never been anywhere in it.

i got behind the wardrobe. between it and the wall, on my side, in a gap that exists because the floor isnt level. that was the best available option in my home and it was not a good one and i knew that while i was doing it.

forty seconds later somebody knocked on my door.

five minutes of knockingwk 17 +1

and it was friendly. thats what i cant get across properly. a big warm voice, the kind that carries, the kind you'd hear across a bar.

"hello? are you home?"

"helloooo?"

five minutes. i counted at the time and i counted again off the building cam after. five minutes and change of a man knocking on my door and calling out like a neighbour returning a parcel, while i was folded into a nine inch gap behind a wardrobe with my heart going hard enough that i was worried about the noise of it.

then, and the shift in tone is the part i keep replaying:

"OKAY. FINE. FUCK YOU."

and they blew the door. properly blew it, a charge, not a boot. my door went across the room and took the corner of the kitchen strip with it.

they found the screen before they found mewk 17 +1

two of them. big. professional enough to bring a charge, unprofessional enough to spend five minutes announcing themselves first.

they went through the room. i heard my own things being moved. and then one of them stopped, and i knew exactly where he was standing, because i knew what was on that screen.

"heh. hide now? in this shithole? where would he hide?"

and he was right. that was the correct read. i was, at that moment, about four feet from him, in the only gap in the room, and if he had turned his head thirty degrees it would have been over.

then my machine restarted again.

SUCK MY COCK
second message. i was four feet away and i saw the light change on the wall.

they lost it. absolutely lost it. they beat my tower and my monitor to pieces, and it was loud and it went on longer than it needed to, and i have thought a lot since about the fact that a man who can pop a head from outside a building chose, at that moment, to type a schoolyard insult instead.

it worked. it took their attention off the room for maybe fifteen seconds and it made them angry, which made them loud, which made them slow.

i am not going to pretend i understood that at the time. at the time i thought i was about to die because of a joke.

"HEY! I KNOW YOU HAVE FUCKING CONTACT WITH THIS MERC! WHERE THE FUCK ARE YOU!"

and there it is. thats the sentence. thats what this was.

somebody read my website. somebody read four months of a man documenting an unkillable merc, and their takeaway was that i must have a phone number.

they threw me into my own wall hard enough that i lost a second or two, and when it came back i was upright against it with a gun in my face and someone shouting.

and then his head came apartwk 17 +1

mid word.

not shot. i need that clear and im the person best qualified in this city to tell you the difference, i have photographed both. a round does directional damage. it takes a path, it takes material with it, theres a channel and theres a side that took it. this had no direction. it went out, evenly, all at once, and i was close enough to be wearing it.

his body stayed up for a moment. then it didnt.

the other one dropped me. i went down on the floor and he was screaming, actually screaming, gun swinging around the room at nothing.

nothing happened. i heard the mechanism do something that wasnt firing, and i watched him look at it, and i watched him understand.

same as the first. same instant, same everything, mid word again, and i think the mid word part is deliberate, i think both of them got exactly as far as they were allowed to get.

ive written a whole evidence section about deaths with no shooter in the room. i built it out of ncpd photos and a coroner's tech and an argument i had with myself for six weeks about whether i was inventing a category.

automatic fire. enormous. through my window, into my apartment, and i went flat and got under the desk frame and stayed there.

a minute. an actual minute. i have never heard anything go that long. plaster and glass coming down the whole time.

then it stopped and i stayed under there for five more, which i timed, because timing something was the only thing i had left that i could control.

it had not been shooting at me. not a round anywhere near where i had been.

and it had not been shooting.

GO TO BED
ILL DEAL THE BODIES
my east wall. approx 1.9m across. every character.

lettered. into my wall. from outside. from a distance, through a window, in one pass, at a rate of fire where the individual impacts are not distinguishable to the ear.

i stood in front of that for a long time.

and heres the detail that finished me off, the one i keep going back to: it says "ill deal the bodies." not "deal with." he dropped a word.

because every character costs rounds. because at that rate, in that time, over that distance, "with" is four more letters and four more letters is a meaningful quantity of ammunition and a meaningful amount of time hanging in a firing position over a residential block.

he edited it. mid-burst, or before, but he edited it down for economy, the way you'd trim a message to fit a limit.

obviously i didnt. i had two bodies on my floor and a message on my wall and the only person in the world who could explain either was somewhere within line of sight of my building, right then, probably still in position.

i went to the window. nothing. i went down the stairwell and out onto the street in the state i was in and stood in the middle of the road turning in circles like an idiot. nothing.

i came back up and i sat on the floor with my back against the door frame where my door used to be and i decided i was going to stay awake until something happened, because i was going to catch him, because after seventeen weeks i had finally been in a room with him and i was not going to let that be it.

i fell asleep.

i fell asleep on my own floor in a room with two dead men in it. thats what my body did. after everything, thats what it decided.

i checked the clock going down and i checked it waking up because thats the kind of thing i do now.

under five minutes. call it four and change.

the bodies were gone.

not covered, not moved to the hall. gone. and everything that had come out of them was gone with it, off my floor, off my wall, off the wardrobe, off my clothes. i checked my own hands and there was nothing on them.

my door was in its frame. hung, aligned, closed. the corner of the kitchen strip it took out was not taken out.

and the wall was blank. no lettering, no holes, no fill, no fresh paint smell, no dust on the floor under where it had been. the same tired grey it has been since i moved in, with the same mark near the skirting where i scraped it moving the desk in.

the window was whole.

i want to lay out what that requires. body removal. a full biological clean. a door rehung and a frame repaired. a window replaced. and structural repair to a plastered wall, which is not a fast job even before you get to matching thirty year old paint that has faded unevenly in one specific room, and which cannot dry in four minutes because the physical world does not permit it.

four minutes. one of which i can account for and three of which i cannot.

that is not one man. i have spent seventeen weeks building a file about one man and tonight is the night that stopped being tenable, because whatever else is true, somebody has a crew, and that crew was standing by, close enough to move on a room while i was unconscious in it.

addendum, later that morningwk 17 +1 · 09:15

slept a bit. woke up with something obvious that i missed at four in the morning, which is what happens.

the jokes. all of them.

the gay club, as a place to summon a man to. the bow on the car. the wink carved into a hand. "suck my cock" typed onto a monitor while two armed men stood in my apartment.

every single one of those is a fifteen year old's joke. not a killer's joke, not a threat dressed as humour. genuinely, specifically, the sense of humour of a teenage boy, and it has not developed in any direction in seventeen weeks of observation.

and then i went and looked at the tracklist again.

three soulja boy tracks. a bloodhound gang song called i hope you die. a track whose title i wouldnt type on a page my sister might read. a band whose entire body of work is titles designed to make somebody's mother close a door. sitting in a carefully sequenced set next to a two hundred year old requiem.

its the same person. obviously its the same person, but i mean the taste is one taste, its not a man with a serious side and a joke side. the fastidiousness and the dick joke are not in tension for him. hes not being ironic. he thinks the requiem is good and he thinks the dick joke is good and he has put the same amount of care into the delivery of both.

ive spent four months trying to work out what kind of thing does this. and the honest answer, tonight, is that he might just be a guy with a really specific sense of humour who is also the most dangerous person in night city, and that those two facts are not connected, and that i have been looking for a profundity that isnt there.

she was on the landing. same step. third one down, the one that gets the sun for about forty minutes in the morning, which is the step she always used.

nine weeks.

and she is well. thats the first thing i want to put down. she is better than she has ever been in the two years i knew her. shes filled out, her coat is right, theres no crust round her eyes, her back leg that used to catch doesnt catch. somebody has been feeding her properly and on a schedule and has had a vet look at her, and i can tell all of that in about four seconds because i spent two years looking at a cat who had none of it.

she came straight over. no hesitation, no wariness, straight over like nine weeks was a long weekend.

third step. 06:14. i did not use a flash and i did not need one.

i stood in a queue for eleven minutes. i paid a hundred eddies out of a wad of money with a joke written on it. and then i went into the busiest venue in heywood on its busiest night of the week and stood at the edge of the floor with a camera in my bag like a man at a school disco.

i did a full circuit. twice. i went up to the level that overlooks the stage, which is where i stood in an empty building six weeks ago listening to a dead man's radio station. there were about forty people up there having a very good night.

nobody was waiting for me. of course nobody was waiting for me.

object onewk 21 · tuesday

theres a feeder in the kitchen.

not a bowl. a unit. programmable, refrigerated, portion controlled, with a scale in the base that weighs her before and after. i looked it up. its top of the line, its the one veterinary practices use for post-op animals, and it costs more than the car i drove for eleven years.

its already programmed. four portions, spaced, and the timings are not arbitrary, theyre the timings of a cat who has spent two years eating whenever a man who works nights happened to be home. somebody watched her eat and then built the schedule around what she already does.

and the food in it is the medical grade stuff. joint support. shes had a bad leg her whole life and it was fixed nine weeks ago by somebody who then, apparently, kept thinking about it afterwards.

i sat on the kitchen floor for a while with that.

hes told me to stop. hes taken the plate off my car and hes come into my house and said my name in a voice with nothing in it. and hes still feeding my cat. hes still, quietly, on a tuesday, eight days into not speaking to me, thinking about her back leg.

im not in the relationship anymore.
she is.

and i understand exactly how that sentence reads and im leaving it up.
