i have thought about almost nothing else since. i have built an entire identity out of being the man who documents things accurately when other people cannot, and i have said it on this website about nine times like it was a virtue and possibly the only one i had left. and the instrument was in the bag. and i just stood there being a person having a conversation.

whatever four and a half months of this has done to me, thats the measurement. thats the number. i was in a room with the only thing that has ever mattered and i behaved like somebody's friend had walked in.

i have a description. a real one. fifty one seconds, daylight, four feet, no obstruction, and the one thing my memory is genuinely trained for is faces at scenes.

i wrote it out the same evening while it was fresh. it is detailed. it is a working description of a specific individual and i am not going to pretend otherwise or be coy about how good it is.

im publishing the parts thats already been on this site since week seventeen. hes young, early twenties. a lot of piercings. the wolf cut. thats it, thats what youre getting, and none of that is new.

the rest of it is in a file that is not on this machine and not in this house.

and heres where i am, and im going to be honest that this is the first time in twenty one weeks i have not been able to make an editorial decision by myself.

the last time i published something he did not want published, i had a warning delivered in my front room in a voice with nothing in it, and there is a folder of consequences i have not seen the end of. sixty two words with no names in them did that.

a working physical description of a man with no photographs in existence is not sixty two words. thats the single most dangerous object anyone has ever assembled about him. thats the thing regina spent six years not doing.

and i also know exactly what i am when i am left alone with a fact. you have all watched me do it for four months. i am not able to trust my own judgement on this one and i would rather say that out loud than pretend i weighed it carefully.

a robot. of him. and its bad. thats the thing i need to convey properly. this is a man who sourced a nine year old computer chassis with a matching dent and machined a hundred thousand bills to a tolerance i measured with calipers, and this thing is cardboard, panel offcuts, actual visible tape, and a moulded face that is recognisably him in the way a child's drawing is recognisably a house.

the road — nine days of nothing

hes not answeringwk 22 · 03:40

four hundred and some frames, taken across three weeks, because i photograph everything, because thats the pathology. every room, every angle, the corridor sightlines, the window a person cannot be seen from, the gap behind the boiler housing that only exists because the floor is not level, which i know because i shot it and i shot it because it was a nice bit of light.

wk 33 — the second one

im going to be careful and slow with this entry because there is more in this photograph than there is in the entire rest of this website, and because i have been wrong about every large object anybody has ever handed me.

i came home on my ownwk 33 · 03:33

two weeks of nothing after the first photograph. i worked. i did four scenes in nine days, one of them a genuinely horrible one out past the wall that had nothing to do with anybody, and i drove home from it at my own pace, on my own decision, with nobody involved.

i pulled up outside my house and looked at the clock before i got out because i always look at the clock, and it said 03:33.

i want to be extremely precise about this because it is the part that has cost me the most sleep and it is not the part anybody will talk about.

i was not woken up. nobody switched me on. there was no lamp, no voice, no wreath. i finished a job, i stopped for food i didnt eat, i took the long way because the short way was closed, and i arrived at my own front door at half three in the morning because that is when i happened to arrive.

  • 01coincidence. it is one minute in a day and i look at that clock forty times a week and i would notice this one every time.
  • 02he knew when i would be home. which requires him to have known the shape of my night before i did, and i have four separate documented instances of him doing exactly that, so this is not a hard one to believe.
  • 03i arrived at it.

03 is the one. i cant prove it and its the one.

3_33 told me in week seventeen that the number was a doorbell and not a message and that i should stop looking for meaning in it. and then in week twenty he took my head in his hand and turned it away from a clock, and i put it back on the board.

seven months in
and i think i go there by myself now.

nobody has to ring a doorbell you have started opening the door for.

wk 51 — one hundred and three

four months of nothing and then three minutes. i have been to all of them. it took me nine days and i have not been able to write it up until now and this is the fourth attempt.

03:33:00wk 51

i had the scanner on because i always have the scanner on. i was not working. i was in the kitchen.

an open hotspot flagged closed. thats normal, it happens maybe forty times a week citywide, a call gets resolved and the flag clears.

then another one. then eleven at once.

then the band did something i have never heard it do in eleven years, which is stop being a series of individual events and become a noise.

03:33:001
03:33:3014
03:34:0032
03:34:3054
03:35:0073
03:35:3092

103 flagged hotspots cleared · elapsed 3 minutes 4 seconds · every district

and then it stopped and the band went back to being a band.

it started at 03:33:00. i want that noted once, at the top, and then i am not going to make it about me.

the arithmeticwk 51 edited ×3

im going to do this properly because it is the only part i can do properly, and because everybody in the comments is going to do it anyway and i would rather have the numbers on the page than in four hundred replies.

cleared, fatal cleared, survivors unrelated

103 sites · 184 seconds · every district including two i have never had a reason to enter

distance
the two furthest sites are 31 kilometres apart by road.
not in a straight line. by road, at night, through a city with junctions in it. thats a twenty six minute drive in a caliburn with nothing in the way and no stops, and it does not include the other hundred and one.
per site
1.78 seconds each. including travel.
not 1.78 seconds of work. 1.78 seconds of everything — arriving, entering, doing whatever was done, and leaving, averaged, with zero time allocated to moving between them.
bodies
i have a confirmed count of 391 and i believe the real number is higher.
higher because at eleven of these sites the remains could not be resolved into individuals by anybody, including the people whose job that is, and the official figures at those eleven are estimates from clothing.
method
and this is the part that stopped me sleeping.
no two sites are the same.
IT IS NOT POSSIBLE
not with a sandevistan. not with two. not with a crew of forty working simultaneously, because a crew of forty leaves forty signatures and there is one.
i have written seven months about a man who does things nobody can do and i have never once had to type this sentence.
i am not offering an explanation. i do not have one. neither does anybody i have asked and i have asked everybody.
i went to all of themwk 51 · nine days

nine days. i slept in the car four of those nights. i shot every site i could get into and i talked my way into eleven i should not have, and i am not going to describe most of what i photographed and i want to explain why rather than be coy about it.

this website has, for eleven months, been able to describe what he does. i have written about wound channels and burn patterns and ricochet geometry and i have been proud of my ability to make a room legible on a page.

i cannot do it with these.

at about forty of the hundred and three there is nothing to describe in the sense i mean it. its material. its a room that has had a quantity of person distributed through it and the word i keep writing and deleting is unrecognisable, and i keep deleting it because it implies there was something to recognise.

ive stood in a lot of rooms. i have never in eleven years had to leave one and sit down outside, and i did that at three separate addresses in the same week.

the room in kabuki in week three, the one i said i couldnt describe and stay professional about — that room is the eightieth worst thing i saw in nine days. it doesnt make the top fifty.

every one of them is differentwk 51

this is the finding. everything else is scale and scale is just a number, and this is the thing that actually tells you something.

i catalogued all hundred and three by method as far as i could establish it, and there is no repetition anywhere in the set.

categorysitesnotes
blade17and not one blade. i can separate at least four distinct edge profiles across the seventeen

a man in a hurry does not do this.

if you have three minutes and a hundred and three addresses you use the fastest thing you have, every time, at every stop, because thats what a hurry is. that is the entire meaning of the word.

he used everything. blade, fist, shotgun, smg, pistol, katana, poison, quickhack, the environment, and at two of them he used nothing at all and left everybody breathing.

he did the complete version.
of his entire kit.
in one hundred and eighty four seconds.

ninety hours of marker on a hundred thousand bills. the album intro nobody needed. the 1989 cassette when a cleaner take exists. all seven tracks. this is that. this is exactly and precisely that, and i have spent eleven months documenting the behaviour that produced it and i still was not ready for what it looks like at scale.

the post-mortem thingwk 51

i have to log this and i want to log it carefully because it is the only genuinely new behaviour in the entire set and because i am not certain about it.

at somewhere between nine and fourteen sites there is damage that i believe occurred after death. limbs removed. remains rearranged. in two cases arranged in a way i am not going to describe.

this is not him. eleven months. two hundred plus documented deaths before this week. i have never once found post-mortem anything, and i have said in print on this website that his efficiency is total and that nothing he does is decorative.

heres the honest uncertainty, which two coroners' techs and one very patient cleaner have all landed on independently:

or
the shotgun and the arms do that anyway.
dismemberment is a documented property of both. a limb coming off during is indistinguishable from a limb coming off after once the room is in that state, and every single one of the ambiguous sites is in the shotgun or blade group.

so: i cannot tell. thats the finding and its unsatisfying and im leaving it unsatisfying rather than picking the version that makes a better entry.

if it is post-mortem then something changed in four months. if it isnt then nothing did and this is just what his whole kit looks like when you use all of it at once in one night.

i want it to be the second one. i am aware that i want it to be the second one. thats in here so you can weight the rest of this entry accordingly.

site 03 — the witnesswk 51 · 04:20

third address i got to, about forty minutes after it cleared. and there was somebody still standing in the street outside.

mid twenties. delivery courier, wrong place, took shelter in the wrong doorway when it started. not injured. not one mark on him that was his own.

he was covered. head to boots. it was in his hair and he had not noticed it was in his hair.

and he was not in shock in the way i have seen four hundred people be in shock. he was elated. he could not stand still. he talked at me for nineteen minutes without me asking a second question and i have transcribed the section that matters exactly as he said it, including the volume, because taking the volume out would be dishonest.

[recorder on. he asked me to record it. he asked twice.]
"HE CAME IN HERE LIKE — YAAAHHH!!!!!!! — BOOM POP POW!!!!!!
[he does the sound effects with his whole body. he is covered in a man.]
THERE WAS FOUR GUYS LEFT AND THEY WERE SWISS CHEESING THIS MERC — AND HE STOOD THERE FOR A SOLID FORTY SECONDS BEING HIT!!!
JUST STOOD THERE!!! TAKING IT!!! AND HE GOES —
'give me a second guys i need to skip these songs on my playlist'
[he does the voice. bored. flat. a man dealing with an interruption.]
IT WAS INSANE!!!! THIS MERC IS GOD PRACTICALLY!!"

i asked him whether he understood what had happened in the building behind him.

he said yes. immediately, no hesitation, and then went straight back to the forty seconds. he came back to the forty seconds eleven times in nineteen minutes. its the only part he wanted to talk about and every time he got to it he got faster.

i asked whether he was frightened at the time.

"nah — no, listen, at the start, yeah, i was under the — i thought i was done, right? but then he clocks me. he clocks me and he does like a — he does a little hand thing. like, stay there. and then he just carries on, and once you know youre not on the list its the best thing you will ever see in your life. im sorry. i know. i KNOW. it is."

and then he asked me if the website was mine, because he recognised me, because he has been reading it since week nine.

i have been publishing for eleven months and this is the first time somebody has known who i was at a scene, and it was a man standing in a street wearing four other people.

hes agreed to be identified as a courier and nothing else and i am holding to that. i offered to take his name out entirely and he was almost offended.

the radiowk 51

at every site with a working speaker system — i make it thirty one of the hundred and three — the station played after.

i have twenty two separate confirmations. i captured six myself off my own dish, which i have now had for forty three weeks and which cost me forty eddies and a shipping crate.

and the sequencing is continuous.

i want to be very precise here because it took me two days to be sure and it is the single strangest data point i have ever put on this website. site 07 ends partway through a track. site 19 picks up in the same track at approximately the point site 07 stopped. site 44 is later in the same record. site 88 is the outro.

it isnt a station playing at a hundred and three places.
its one continuous play, moving.

he was listening to a record. and he did all of it, everywhere, in the order the record played.

which would mean the run is not a hundred and three jobs. its one thing, and it lasted the length of a side.

wk 52 — september 28

one year. i did not know it was one year. somebody in the guestbook told me and then somebody else told me the other thing, and ive had to sit down twice writing this.

the site was gone againwk 52 · 03:33

same as week fifteen. every section, every log, the board, the guestbook, all of it. no CSS, no template, no nav. one page.

and i knew what it was before my eyes focused, because i have seen this exact white page once before and it has been in my head for nine months.

he did not upgrade the bit. thats the first thing i want to say about it. a man who built a functioning braindance and lettered a wall with a machine gun and spent ninety hours on a marker joke opened his second defacement in a year with the same cheap trick.

thats the whole page.

eleven exclamation marks. i counted them, obviously i counted them, i counted the seven on the lockscreen in a nightclub and i counted these on my kitchen floor.

and the signature is four and a half lines down and slightly indented and not aligned to anything.

i want to be precise about why that detail got me, because it will look like sentiment and it isnt. that is not a design decision. thats a man who does not know how to lay out a page pressing return until it looked far enough away from the other thing. its the same hand as LOVE YA in red marker and its the same hand that wrote a name on the bottom of a plastic dinosaur.

he has never once, in any medium, tried to make his own handwriting look like anything other than his.

he built a playerwk 52

theres a song on the page. and he did not link it. he did not point at it. he implemented a small grey rectangle with a play button and a progress bar, badly, in the ugliest possible way, so that one file would play for one person.

the file is a track by an act that is already on his station. its been on my week seventeen tracklist for nine months and i wrote its title down and moved on and never listened to it properly.

and i want to describe what it actually is, because everyone reading this is about to press the button and i think you should know what youre pressing.

the first minute is a grown man making car noises. thats it. thats the whole first minute — engine sounds, revving, done with his mouth, badly, with total commitment. no irony in it at all. its the noise a nine year old makes with a toy.

and then it becomes a birthday song, and the birthday song is about something horrible.

im not going to transcribe the words and im going to say why rather than leave it hanging. its his. its off his station, its the second time in a month i have had the option to take a piece of music apart on this website and publish the anatomy of it, and im not going to do it twice.

press the button or dont. its four minutes. i have listened to it about forty times now and i have not decided anything.

the bass on it is genuinely extraordinary, by the way. i know nothing about music. i have been told by four people in the guestbook already and all four of them used the word eleven.

the first thing anybody has ever told mewk 52 · 06:00

a year.

everything on this website i took. i paid a fixer in dogtown for a photograph of a plate. i paid regina and she wouldnt take the money. i sat in a vent for forty minutes. i went to a hundred and three addresses in nine days. every single fact in four hundred thousand words is a thing i extracted, was handed as a consequence, or had done to me.

nobody asked him anything. there was no question on the table. there was no leverage and nothing to trade and no way to have got it out of him.

its his birthday.
thats the first thing he has ever just told me.

a year of a man who does not explain himself, who has never once been in a room for the part where somebody answers him, who says things in a dead voice or through a cat or in red marker and leaves before you can respond.

and on the anniversary of the day i started writing about him, he took the whole site down to say four words about himself, in a font he didnt pick, with a signature he couldnt centre.

and then put a song on it.

and then archivist_wren postedwk 52 · 09:40

i had the entry three quarters written. i was going to end it on the paragraph above, and it was a good ending, and it was the wrong one.

somebody in the guestbook pulled the timestamp off entry 000.

28 september, 02:17.

this website is exactly one year old today. to the day. entry 000 went up at seventeen minutes past two in the morning on the twenty eighth of september, after a night at the riverfront address, and it opens with me saying i started keeping notes because the details wouldnt sit still in my head.

and this morning he took the whole thing down to tell me it is his birthday.

so put those next to each other.

i started writing about him
on his birthday.

by accident. completely by accident, with no possible way of knowing, because nobody on this planet knew that fact until 03:33 this morning and the only person who did has never told anybody anything.

i did not pick that night. a scanner picked it. three people died on the riverfront and i drove there and photographed a room and came home and could not sleep and opened a text file at two in the morning, and that is the entire origin of this website, and it landed on the twenty eighth of september because thats when the call came in.

a man got a birthday present in the form of a stranger beginning a permanent public record of his life, and neither of them found out for a year.

except he did find outwk 52 · 14:00

obviously he found out. thats the part.

he has had root on this server since about week two. he read entry 000 the same week i wrote it and it is date stamped at the top of the page in a font i did not choose either.

so he has known, for eleven and a half months, that the file on him opened on his birthday.

and he did nothing with it. not in week fifteen when he emptied a club. not in week seventeen when he lay on my bed and made three jokes and gave me a house. not in week twenty two when he built a city and put a sixteen day joke in it. not once, in a year, in any of the four hundred thousand words either of us have been in.

he waited for the anniversary.

a full year of setup, held, in silence, through everything, so that four words in times new roman would land on the correct morning.

ive said it about ninety hours of marker. ive said it about seven tracks and an album intro and a 1989 cassette. tape_hiss has said it about nine times and apologised for making it sound endearing.

this is the longest one. this is the longest setup in the entire file and the payoff is a webpage he could not centre.

which leaves the thing i cant dowk 52 · 23:00

same day.

and i have been at this for a year and i know exactly what i am looking at, which is an object with no answer in it, and i have already had four days of my life taken by a tub of ice cream and i am not doing that again.

so heres the whole list, once, and then im leaving it.

  • 01its genuinely his birthday and the overlap is a coincidence. one day in three hundred and sixty five, a scanner call decided it, and things like this happen to people constantly and mean nothing.
  • 02its genuinely his birthday, the overlap is a coincidence, and he found it funny enough to hold for a year. this is the one i think is true and i have no way to establish it.
  • 03its not his birthday. he saw the date on entry 000, decided it was the funniest available thing to do with a date, and has quietly had a birthday on the twenty eighth of september ever since.

i cannot eliminate any of them and i am not going to try and i want it on record that i stopped at three and did not write a fourth.

what i will say is that 03 does not disqualify anything. if he read a date off a webpage and decided it was his, thats not a lie. thats how he does everything. he takes a thing, decides what a better version of it would be, and keeps that instead, and he does not ask.

i have had that written on my board since week twenty one and i did not once consider that it might apply to a date.

and if 03 is what happened then it means the only birthday he has is one he took off the front of a website somebody made about him.

i have thought about that sentence for nine hours and i am not going to write a paragraph underneath it.

the site came back up at about ten past four, complete, to the character, same as last time.

hes twenty one today, if any of it is real. theres a song on my kitchen laptop about a man who has lost the use of his legs. the cat is asleep on the good chair.

— lou

wk 54 — the second witness

the longest interview i have ever done. four hours across two days and he asked for the second one. im publishing about a third of it and the rest stays with me and hes seen exactly what is going up.

who he iswk 54

building maintenance. forty six. eleven years in the same block, which is a working residential in a district im not naming, eighty odd units, mostly families and mostly people on shifts.

hes agreed to be described as the caretaker and nothing else, and unlike the courier he did not have to be talked into that, he asked for it first thing and then checked twice that i meant it.

i want to establish something before any of the rest of this, because everybody is going to read this entry for the wrong part.

a crew took his building. not a gang with a corner, an actual crew, the kind that arrives with a list. they were in there for most of an evening before anything else happened, and in that time they killed four people who lived there.

he knew all four. one of them for eleven years.

the caretaker did not come to me to talk about the man with the knives. he came to me because of the names page and because he wanted four people written down properly, and everything below is what he told me on the way to that.

theyre up. theyre the first four on the wk 54 block on and he checked every spelling himself.

where he waswk 54

a service void behind the second floor riser cupboard. hes the only person in that building who knows its big enough to get into, because hes the only person who has ever had to get into it.

he could see about four metres of corridor through the gap where the panel doesnt sit flush. he has been meaning to fix that panel for two years.

he was in there roughly ninety minutes. what follows happened in the last four of them.

the first onewk 54

they had three men from the building on their knees in that corridor. one of them had a weapon against his face.

interview · the caretaker · day one · excerpt
him"i was watching the one with the gun. i was watching his hands because thats where it was going to come from."
[long pause. he does this a lot. the courier could not stop talking and this man stops constantly.]
him"and there was a—"
[he makes the noise. he made it eleven times over two days and it is always exactly the same noise and he is always slightly embarrassed afterwards.]
SHIIINKKK— and he went down like a bag.
him"straight down. not backwards, not sideways. down. and theres a handle sticking out the back of his head and i did not see it arrive. i was looking at him and i did not see it arrive."
me"what did the men on their knees do."
him"nothing. nobody did anything. it was too quiet. thats what nobody understands, its that there was no noise at all, so nobody knew to start being frightened yet."

and then it kept happening.

SHIIINKKKthud.
SHINKthud.
SHIIINKKKthud.

he could not see most of them. thats the detail that has stayed with me out of four hours of tape. he had four metres of corridor and almost all of it was happening somewhere else, so what he actually experienced was a sound, repeating, at irregular intervals, from different distances, and each one meaning a person had stopped.

"you start counting. you dont decide to. i got to nine and then i lost it and started again at one, and i know that isnt how counting works."

the one who worked it outwk 54

eventually somebody found a body.

interview · day one · excerpt
him"he starts shouting. hes about two metres from the panel. and hes going—"
"EVERYBODY — SOMEBODIES FUCKING HERE!!"
him"and im thinking, right, thats it, because now theyre going to go through this whole floor properly, and theres one place on this floor to hide and im in it and i built it."
"KEEP AN EYE OUT! FUCKING FIND HI—"
SHIINKKKthud.
[mid-word. the caretaker is very precise about this and repeated it on day two unprompted, in the same place, with the same cut-off.]
him"he never finished the word. i keep thinking about that. hes the only one who worked out what was happening and he got about two thirds of a sentence."

four seconds later, the roof.

there was a marksman up there. the caretaker knew because he had watched him go up ninety minutes earlier and had spent the entire time in the void being aware of him.

SHIIINKKK

…and then a long noise. he described it as a whistle and a rush at the same time and it took him a while to place it.

THUD. SPLAT.

he came off the roof. four storeys, past the gap in the panel, and the caretaker saw about a tenth of a second of him going past and heard the rest.

"i have been up on that roof a thousand times. its a hard climb, theres no ladder anymore, you have to go through the plant room. four seconds after the shouting one stopped. four."

the last onewk 54

one left. the one running it.

the caretaker described him twice on two different days without prompting and both descriptions match: very large, full sleeve of chrome on both arms, and carrying a belt-fed weapon that he estimated at about a metre and a half.

he was moving down the corridor slowly, checking doors. he was about six feet from the panel.

interview · day two · excerpt
him"and then it was just—"
[he does the noise five times, fast, no gaps, which is the only time in four hours he does it more than once in a row.]
SHINK SHINK SHINK SHINK SHINK
him"and hes in bits on the floor. and i mean in bits, i mean legs and arms and — it wasnt messy. thats the thing i cant. it was in five pieces and it was tidy."
me"how long between the first noise and the last."
him"…theres no gap. its one noise with five bits in it."

in that order · confirmed twice on separate days · no other damage anywhere on the body

i want to make a point about this and then leave it, because it is the only genuinely analytical thing i have to add to a man's testimony and i dont want to bury him under it.

one of those five is sufficient. the head is sufficient. any of the others alone would end the fight.

five is not efficiency. five is not a spray either, because a spray does not produce five clean separations in a specific order with nothing else touched. five, in that sequence, is a decision that was made and then executed in less time than the witness could register as time.

and the man being taken apart was, by every physical measure, the largest and best-armed person in that building.

and then he was therewk 54

the caretaker was still looking at the floor when a man appeared standing over it.

not walked in. appeared. optical camo dropping is documented on this website eleven times and every witness describes it the same way, which is as an absence stopping.

interview · day two
him"hes small."
[this is the first thing he said about him, on both days, before anything else.]
him"the one on the floor was a big unit. and this lad is — hes nothing. hes skinny. hes shorter than me and im not a tall man. that gun on the floor next to him is nearly as long as he is."
him"and hes covered. head to foot. you couldnt tell what colour anything he had on was."
me"what did he do first."
him"looked round. left to right."
[he demonstrates it. he turns his head at a constant rate, no pauses, no saccades, all the way left to all the way right, and stops dead. it does not look like a person looking at a room. i asked him to do it twice and i wish i hadnt.]
him"like a camera on a mount. like when the head does it and nothing else does."
me"and then he saw you."
him"and then he stopped. on the panel. on the gap. and i thought, well, thats me."

and instead:

"he grinned at me. big grin. the way you do when youve been caught doing something daft. and he did the little—"

✌

"—off his eyebrow, like that, and he goes hello! and thats it. thats the whole thing. and then he got on with what he was doing."

the caretaker was in that void for a further nineteen minutes and the man never came back to it and never looked at it again.

what he did for nineteen minuteswk 54

he looted the place.

thats not a euphemism and im not softening it. he went through the crew methodically, took what was on them, went through their vehicle, and then went through two of the units the crew had already been through, which the caretaker was very careful to point out to me twice.

"he didnt turn over any flats they hadnt already done. i want that said. he did the ones that were already open."

i asked whether that seemed deliberate. he said he had thought about nothing else for nine days and that he could not tell me whether it was consideration or just efficiency and that it had stopped mattering to him which one.

and the whole time, for nineteen minutes, the caretaker could hear him.

interview · day two · the last thing he told me
him"he was singing. under his breath. the whole time."
me"could you make out words."
him"not really. it was the same bit over and over. it was like—"
"yaah… yaahh… bitch! yaaahh……"
[he does it quietly, tunelessly, in the exact cadence of a person half-remembering a song while doing something with their hands.]
him"just to himself. like a lad doing the washing up."
which settles wk 53wk 54

a fortnight ago a track appeared on his station for the first time in a year, and i wrote that i could not establish whether the courier had heard it playing or heard the man himself.

i can establish it now.

he hums it. hes had it in his head for at least a month, hes been doing it under his breath while working, and the courier at site 03 three weeks earlier heard the same thing at volume coming through a door and reproduced it back at me as a sound effect, and thirty thousand people put it on a shirt.

its not a battle cry.
its a song he cant get out of his head.

and it has been in his head long enough that he went and found the version of it he wanted, and put it on a station that had not changed in a year.

im going to say the thing plainly and then stop.

the caretaker watched a man dismantle nine people in four minutes without being seen, then drop his camo, do a two finger salute to a stranger in a hole in a wall, and tidy up for nineteen minutes humming a seventy year old song to himself.

i have four hours of tape and eleven months of file and thats the most complete picture anybody has ever got, and it is not a picture of a soldier or a psychopath or a weapon.

its a picture of somebody at work.

— lou

wk 56 — the car park

i was not there. i want that first, before anything else, because everything below is assembled out of eleven accounts from people who were, and i have never had to write an entry this way before.

i found out at 04:20wk 56

i was asleep. actually asleep, in a bed, for the first time in nine days, which i had been quite pleased about.

i woke up to the guestbook doing something i have not seen it do since the hundred and three, and the first eleven comments were all people who had been standing in the same car park two hours earlier.

the car park behind dicky twisters. vista del rey.

im going to let that sit for a second because everybody who has read this website for more than a month just made the same noise i did.

thats the one he emptied in week fifteen to leave a message on every screen. thats the one he sent me to on a friday in week eighteen so he could call me a dumbass on my own lockscreen. its the one building in this city that means something to both of us and it is the only place i have ever been that he chose.

he went back to it at three in the morning and put on a show.

what was therewk 56 · 03:00

a drum machine. a microphone on a stand. a small amp stack. and a guitar.

every single one of the eleven accounts describes the guitar first and every single one of them recognised it, and four of them used the same phrase without having read each other, which is that it was the one.

im not going to do the analysis on that. its the third of them now. theres the weapon from week six and week thirty three, theres the vehicle in both photographs, and now theres this, and i said in week thirty three that i would stop where the evidence stopped and i am holding to it.

what i will say is that a man who does not explain himself has now been photographed with two of them and has performed in front of two hundred and fifty people with the third.

no crew. no security. nobody on a door. one person setting up a drum machine on the tarmac at three in the morning behind a closed club.

and then he startedwk 56 · 03:04

slam.

brutal slamming death metal, played live, by one person, in a car park in vista del rey, in the year 2077.

i have had four separate people explain to me over the last eighteen hours why that sentence is more absurd than it looks, and tape_hiss has done it best and hes going to do it again in the comments so ill keep this short.

that genre has not been performed live in this city in living memory. it has not been performed live anywhere in a very long time. its on his station — its most of a cluster on his station — and every last piece of it is at minimum fifty years old and most of it is seventy, and it exists now the way a language exists when the last speakers have died: in recordings, held by people who kept them.

and he stood in a car park and played it.

hes not preserving the archive anymore.
hes producing it.

the crowdwk 56

nobody announced it. i have checked every board, every channel i have access to, and i have asked eleven people directly. there was no notice. there was a man in a car park with an amp at three in the morning and then there was this.

03:045
03:0710
03:1120
03:1650
03:22100
03:31250
estimates reconciled across eleven accounts · nobody was counting · everybody agrees on 250

and they went up. every account uses a version of the same sentence, which is that it took about ninety seconds for the first five people to work out that it was allowed.

there was a pit. by 03:20 there was a pit going in a car park in vista del rey with a hundred people in it and by half past there were two hundred and fifty and it was, by every description i have, absolutely brutal.

"i have not seen anything like that in my life and i am fifty one years old and i used to go to things."

and some of the people in that car park will have known somebody on the names page. i did not put that sentence in the first version of this entry because i was busy being wry about myself, and teodora put it in the guestbook within the hour, and it belongs here in the body and not as a note at the bottom.

people got hurt. i want that in here rather than left out. seven of the eleven mention blood and three mention it being on them and none of them mention anybody being unhappy about it, and one of them told me she has a broken finger and that it was worth it, and i have chosen to include that sentence and let you decide what to do with it.

what he playedwk 56

as far as anybody can reconstruct it, and this is nine people cross-checking each other over eighteen hours:

reconstructed · approximate order · gaps where nobody could agree
  1. opener — nobody could identify it. four people think it was not a cover.
  2. from the station · cluster two, the slam block
  3. from the station · cluster two
  4. unidentified · two people describe it as "the long one"
  5. from the station · cluster two
  6. from the station · cluster four, the one with seven tracks
  7. unidentified
  8. from the station · cluster two
  9. closer — cut off. see below.
at least five of nine are material already on 69.420. he did not play anything that is not, as far as anybody can establish, from his own collection.

he played his own record collection. live. by himself. to two hundred and fifty strangers who did not know it existed.

a year ago i wrote that the station was the only part of him that was not about anybody else. i have had to update that sentence twice now and this is the third and it is the biggest.

the only thing he had that was just his, and this month he let a stranger's edit into it, and then he took the whole thing outside and played it to a car park.

03:41wk 56

ncpd.

two units, then four. sirens on approach, which in that district at that hour means they had no idea what they were coming to.

he stopped mid-song. every account is emphatic about this — not finished, stopped, one bar into something.

and then the thing that all eleven of them lead with, before the ending, before the guitar, before anything:

"the crowd moved. two hundred and fifty people and nobody said anything and they just opened up. straight down the middle. like the sea."

not scattered. not ran. opened, in a line, from the front of the crowd to where he was standing, and then stood still on either side of it.

i have four separate people describing that and i have asked all four whether anybody organised it and all four said no and two of them said they did not remember deciding to move.

so at 03:41 there was a straight open corridor of tarmac in a car park in vista del rey with two hundred and fifty people standing along it, and ncpd walking down it, and one person at the end of it holding a guitar.

the endingwk 56 · 03:41:xx

this happened, by consensus, in under four seconds. no two accounts have the order exactly the same and i have gone with the version that seven of eleven agree on.

01
one round from the shotgun, straight up.
nobody was hit. every account is clear on that. it was fired vertically into the air over an empty part of the lot and it was, in the words of one witness, "the loudest thing that has ever happened to me."
02
he took his clothes off.
all of them. in the same movement. i have had this described to me eleven times and i still do not understand the mechanics of it and neither does anybody who was there.
03
and threw them at ncpd.
at them. not away, not down. four officers walking down a corridor of two hundred and fifty people received a man's entire outfit at close range.
04
"THANK YOU, EVERYONE!"
shouted. all eleven have it. two of them have it word for word identical and the other nine are within a word.
05
gone.
camo. mid-lot, in front of two hundred and fifty people and four officers, and that was the last anybody saw of him.

the guitar was still there. so was the drum machine, the amp and the microphone. all of it was left where it was and ncpd took all of it and i have no information about where any of it is now and i am not going to go looking.

nobody was arrested. two hundred and fifty people were still standing in a car park with the lights on them and by every account they simply left, in an orderly way, over about ten minutes, and one witness described it as "like after anything else."

the part i keep coming back towk 56 · 22:00

thirty seven minutes. thats how long he was visible, uncloaked, standing under lights in front of an audience that grew to two hundred and fifty people.

i have had fifty one seconds.

in a year and a quarter, four visits, two photographs, one recording, a cat, and a hundred and three addresses, the total time i have spent in a room with that man with my eyes open is fifty one seconds in an afternoon, and a hundred and eighty people who were walking home from a shift got thirty seven minutes on a tuesday because they heard a noise.

im not upset about it. i want to be clear about that, because a version of me from about eight months ago would have been and would have written four thousand words about what it meant.

hes stopped hiding. thats all this is. he did not stop hiding for me and he did not do it to make a point at me, he did it because at some point in the last two months it stopped being worth the effort, and the first thing he did with the free time was go and play his records to strangers in a car park.

a year of documenting a man nobody could see.
and now two hundred and fifty people have.

the file is not the only record of him anymore. as of tuesday there are two hundred and fifty people in this city who were there, and eleven of them are in my guestbook, and none of them needed me to tell them what happened.

thats the job going away. im not sad about that either. i have a page with seventy two names on it that is nowhere near finished and that nobody else is making.

— lou

wk 57 — the door

im going to write this in the order it happened to me, which means the first two sections are going to feel like nothing. they were nothing at the time. thats the point.

i thought it was himwk 57 · 19:40

came home from a scene. the front door was open about a foot and the lock was destroyed.

not picked. not forced quietly. the mechanism is in three pieces and one of them was in the hallway and the frame is split from the strike plate to the top hinge.

and i stood there and i was irritated.

thats the honest reaction and its the one im going to have to live with. i looked at a destroyed door in my own house and my first complete thought was hes done something again, followed immediately by working out whether i was going to be able to get a locksmith at eight at night, and then a genuine flicker of curiosity about what was going to be inside.

a year and a half of this and a busted door reads to me as an announcement.

so i went in looking for it. thats what i did. i walked through my own house checking for the joke.

checked
the fridge. the tub was where i left it, unopened, square to the front.
checked
the desk. nothing on it. no photograph, no object, nothing square to anything.
checked
the machine. on, untouched, no message.
checked
every room. nothing taken. i have a box in the spare room with ninety four thousand eurodollars in it and it has not been moved.

and it took me about four minutes to work out what was wrong, because it was an absence and not a thing.

no meow.

she does it when the door goes. every time, without exception, for fourteen months. it is the single most reliable event in my life.

the feeder was full. her step was empty. shes not in this house.

and he didnt do itwk 57

i want to lay out why i knew that inside about a minute, because it is the only piece of actual reasoning i have contributed to this entire week.

01
he has never damaged anything of mine.
not once in a year and a half. he has come into this house four times, plus however many i dont know about, and the only thing he has ever broken was a computer he replaced inside four minutes with a better one.
02
he does not need a door.
this is the man who got into a flat behind a caretaker with a working lock, and installed a speaker system in my walls without me noticing for four weeks. a destroyed lock is what somebody does when they cannot do what he does.
03
and he would not take her.
he gave her back. week seventeen. nine weeks and a fixed leg and better optics than mine. she is, of everything on this website, the one thing i am certain he would not do this with.

so somebody else has been in my house.

and that has never happened, and i did not have a reaction available for it, and i spent the first night sitting on the floor by the front door with the bat because there was no lock on it.

the weekwk 57 → wk 58

i looked. obviously i looked. i did what im good at and it produced nothing.

i canvassed the street. i pulled what feeds there are in that district and there are almost none. i sat with the guestbook and about four hundred people offered to help and eleven of them actually did something and i want their names off this page and in a message instead.

birdie made calls. she made a lot of calls and she called in things she should not have called in for a cat and i have told her so and she told me to shut up.

nothing. seven days, nothing.

and no contact from him either. i want that recorded because everybody is going to ask. no visit, no screen, no lockscreen, nothing on the desk. seven days of the same silence as any other week.

i want to be accurate about what that week was like and the accurate version is that i did not sleep and i did not work and i posted nothing here and i was, for the first time since february, of no use to anybody at all.

and then the citywk 58 · thursday

the first one i saw myself was on the overpass at sixth. i was driving under it and i looked up because everybody was looking up.

— every board. no logo. no animation. no explanation. —
DONTFUCKWITHWK8.COM
white text. black field. thats the entire creative.

i have counted thirty six and i am certain that is low.

corporate plaza. the big vista del rey board. four separate transit sites. the two on the expressway approach. print, as well — flyposted, properly, in volume, in at least five districts. and it went out on broadcast, in slot, mid-programme, as a thirty second card with no sound.

i do not know how you buy that. i genuinely do not. i have asked two people who work adjacent to media and both of them said the same thing, which is that you cannot, not in a week, not simultaneously, not without months of booking and a great deal of paperwork with names on it.

and there it is on thirty six boards.

im not going to investigate the how. i have said that about four things now and this is the one i mean the most, because the how does not matter and the what is already up there in ten foot letters.

the sitewk 58 · thursday

its a red room.

for anybody who has been lucky: thats the format. theres a whole miserable genre of them. a page, a feed, a chat, a donate button. most of them are fake. the format exists because people click it.

this is not that format done well or done cleverly. it is that format done plainly. no header, no branding, no name, no explanation, no styling past the necessary. a red page, a camera panel, a chat, four donate buttons.

the video does not resolve. it did not resolve for me and it has not resolved for anybody i have asked, and there is an error where the picture should be, and i have gone back and forth on whether that is deliberate and i have landed on yes and i am not able to prove it.

the audio works.

theres a man in a chair. hes been there the whole time. hes screaming, and nothing in that room ever answers him, and the thing he screams more than anything else is that it was just a cat.

and hes right.
thats the part.
hes completely right and it does not matter at all.

why im putting it herewk 58 · 23:00

ive covered a face twice. i killed a written description and never opened the file again. i refused to identify a record twice, once for him. i took a word out of an entry because somebody explained to me what it cost her.

im not doing that here and i want to be exact about why, because it is not a change of principle and i do not want credit for one.

every single one of those was mine to withhold. i had the only copy. withholding it meant it did not exist.

this is on thirty six billboards.

a hundred thousand people had seen it before i finished my first cup of coffee. its on the plaza screen. its on television. children have read that url out loud on the way to school.

i cannot make this less public. that option is not on the table and it was never on the table, and the only thing left that i can actually do is keep an accurate record of what it was, in the first hour, before it becomes whatever it becomes, because in about a week there will be nine competing versions of tonight and eight of them will be wrong.

so ive archived it. the first hour, as it was, static.

the buttons dont work. the chat doesnt update. the counter doesnt move. the camera never worked in the first place.

theres no violence in it. i want that said before anybody clicks. hes alone in there for the whole hour. thats what the hour is.

the last minute of my capturewk 58

at 58 minutes and 2 seconds theres a door mechanism. distant, not in the room, and it is the first sound in an hour that is not the man in the chair.

and he says no, six times, quietly, which is the only quiet thing he says in the entire hour.

i stopped recording at one hour and fourteen seconds.

im not going to tell you i stopped for a reason. i stopped because i had been sitting in front of it for an hour and my hands were doing something and i pressed the thing and then i sat there for a while longer.

the site is still up. its up right now, while im typing this, and it has been up for eleven hours, and i have not looked at it again.

shes alive. i want to end on that because its the only thing i know and somebody in that chat knew it before i did. shes alive and shes safe and thats not speculation.

and i have not got her back.

wk 59 — thanks4thamoneysuckas.fun

the boards came back. same thirty six positions. and this one i can verify, because the money actually moved and the people it moved to are in my guestbook.

same boards, same nightwk 59 · thursday

eleven days after the last set came down, all thirty six went back up with a new url on them.

same positions. same creative — white text, black field, no logo, no animation, no explanation. corporate plaza, the vista del rey board, the two on the expressway approach, print in five districts, and the broadcast slot.

and the url is THANKS4THAMONEYSUCKAS.FUN, which took me about four seconds to read and about a day to stop being angry about.

the page is raw html. no styling, no template, times new roman, a horizontal rule, a link that closes it. exactly the same as week fifteen and exactly the same as september the twenty eighth. third time. he has never once upgraded the bit.

the signature is three lines down and indented and aligned to nothing. same hand. same as LOVE YA in red marker and the same as a name on the bottom of a plastic dinosaur.

and the last line is a postscript, and the postscript is meow, which is the first word he ever said out loud to anybody on this website, at half three in the morning, in my bedroom, thirteen months ago.

it was realwk 59 · friday

i want to be careful here because this is the first time in eighteen months i have been able to independently verify something he said, and i have never had that before, and it turns out to feel very strange.

the money went.

the families
i have direct confirmation from eleven households.
every one of them is a family i have spoken to while building the names page. every one of them received a payment in a window of about ninety minutes on the wednesday night. it arrived clean — traceable origin, documented, nothing anybody has to explain to anybody. i have had two people read the paperwork and both said the same thing, which is that it looks like a settlement.
the amounts
not equal, and this is the part i cannot stop looking at.
they vary. and as far as i can reconstruct from eleven data points, they vary by household need and not by anything else. the largest went to a family with medical debt. the smallest went to a household that does not have any.
the shelters
four that i have confirmed, all no-kill, all small.
one of them is a two-room operation run out of the back of a laundrette by three volunteers. the amount they received is more than their total intake for the last six years combined and one of them has posted about it in my guestbook and i have left it exactly as she wrote it.

and i did not get anything, before anybody asks. im not a family and im not a shelter. i want that in writing.

he sorted three hundred and ninety one dead people into households and worked out which ones had medical debt. that is not a gesture. thats a fortnight of somebody's evenings.

and then the last paragraphwk 59

and in the middle of all that, in the same breath, in capitals, is a plan to bomb a building with people inside it.

im not going to soften it and im not going to treat it as rhetorical, because on this website the things he says in capitals as jokes have a documented tendency to happen.

four no-kill shelters got money. and every other shelter in this city read the same sentence i did on thursday morning.

ive had three of them contact me since and i am not going to say which or where. two of them wanted to know whether i thought it was serious. one of them had already started moving animals out.

i told all three the same thing, which is the only honest thing i have: i have eighteen months of file on this man and i cannot find a single instance of him saying he would do something and then not doing it.

he gave away a fortune, correctly,
and threatened to kill people,
in the same document,
and signed it meow.

and i have written four hundred thousand words on this website and that is still, somehow, the most complete summary of him that exists.

— lou

wk 60 — what he would actually get

this is not mine. a public defender in this city read eighteen months of my website and built a charging document out of it, the way it would actually be built, and then explained to me why none of it matters. im publishing the whole thing with her permission and her handle on it.

where this came fromwk 60

somebody in the guestbook asked what he would get if he were caught. its a question i have had maybe forty thousand times and always ignored, because it felt like fantasy and because i am a photographer.

pd_marchetti has been reading since about week thirty and has posted eleven times, all of them short, all of them correcting somebody about procedure. twenty two years a public defender in this city.

she sent me a forty page document. this is the summary of it and she has checked this version.

and she told me at the top of the email, before any of the rest of it, that i was going to be disappointed by the ending, and she was right, and i want that flagged here so nobody reads the numbers below and thinks they are the answer.

"the exposure is theatre. i will build it for you properly because you asked properly. then i will tell you what happens in this city, which is nothing."

the part that surprised mewk 60

the largest single block of exposure on that sheet is not the murder.

its the billboards.

three hundred and sixty years, from thirty six counts of unauthorised access to broadcast infrastructure, at ten a piece.

marchetti was blunt about why and it is the most cyberpunk sentence anybody has ever said to me:

"murder is one count. the boards are thirty six counts because thirty six separate corporate entities own them, and every one of those entities has standing, and every one of them will file. a body has one family and they are usually poor. a billboard has shareholders."

and the second largest block is the stalking file. mine. one hundred and thirty five years from nine burglary counts, plus another hundred and something across the rest of it.

ive been documenting a man for eighteen months and the only reason a prosecutor would ever be able to build a case is that i did that. the file is the evidence. i built it, i published it weekly, and i timestamped everything, and marchetti told me it is the single most complete surveillance record on a living person she has ever been handed.

i have spent a year and a half worrying about whether the site puts him at risk. turns out it does. just not in the way i was worried about.

and now the ending she warned me aboutwk 60

none of it happens. heres her reasoning, compressed, and i have not softened any of it.

01
the biggest thing he has ever done is not a crime.
three hundred and ninety one people in one night, and the exposure on it is about two hundred and sixty years of secondary charges, because clearing a flagged hotspot is a job this city advertises and pays for. she said the 103 would be a difficult prosecution and an easy defence and that she has run harder cases about stolen cars.
02
theres no complainant.
the man in the chair is dead and his family is in no position to press anything. i am the complainant on the entire stalking block and i will not testify, and marchetti pointed out — correctly, and i had not thought about it once — that i have publicly stated on this website nine separate times that i was not frightened and that i took no action. she called that "eighteen months of the defendant's best character evidence, published weekly by the victim."
03
theres no chain of custody on anything.
my archives are inadmissible. my photographs are inadmissible. my ballistics are a man with a camera and a hobby. she was kind about it and then said the word "hobby" twice more.
04
and there is no arrest.
this is the one she spent four paragraphs on. NCPD filed a report on the hundred and three that says the individual was not located, about a man who was under lights in a car park for thirty seven minutes six weeks earlier. she said the department has made a decision, and that the decision is not written down anywhere, and that everybody in the building knows what it is.

so what actually happens to him.

she gave me three and said the first is overwhelmingly the most likely, and this is where it stopped being a legal document and started being about the city.

A
nothing. indefinitely.
he continues. the file grows. nobody moves, because moving means somebody has to be the officer who moved, and there is no promotion at the end of that and there is a very clear other outcome. she gave this one about seventy percent.
B
an offer.
not an arrest. a contract, or an acquisition, or whatever the current word is. she said four separate entities have almost certainly already run the numbers on what he is worth and that the only thing stopping them is that nobody has worked out how you would make the approach. twenty five percent.
C
a kill order, unattributed, executed by contractors.
no trial, no charges, no record, and a four paragraph statement afterwards that does not use the word. five percent, and she said the five percent has been climbing since the billboards and that it climbed again when the second set went up.

1,198 years and fifteen life terms,
and the realistic outcome is a job offer.

ive read her document four times now. the thing i cannot get past is not the number and its not the ending.

its that the single most chargeable thing this man has ever done, out of everything — out of fifty one hours in a room, out of three hundred and ninety one people, out of a fourteen year old with two dead parents — is thirty six billboards.

a body has one family and they are usually poor. a billboard has shareholders.

im going to go back to the names page now. thats a hundred and something households who are never going to see any of this, and its the only document about any of this that anybody is ever going to be able to file.

— lou

wk 62 — he came round

first time in a room with him since week twenty three. hes told me to log it, out loud, unprompted, which has never happened before, so this is the first entry on this website he has actually agreed to.

i shot himwk 62 · 01:50

i was reading comments. thats what i was doing. sat in the chair with the machine on my knees going through the wk 60 thread.

THUD. BANG. CRACK.

the outer door. the new one, the good one, the one i had fitted after the last time somebody came through it.

and then whoever it was could not work out the inner door. banging, scraping, a lot of it, from somebody not walking properly. i had about nine seconds and i spent all nine of them with the iron up and my finger on the trigger thinking theyve come back.

the door opens. i fired three, centre mass, before i had processed anything about who was in the frame.

and then:

"louuu… youre a… fuckinh… dickhead… you jknkowthatt…?"

nothing. not a mark, not a stagger, not a change in his footing. i have documented the mitigation on this website for eighteen months and this is the first time i have contributed to the dataset personally.

i shot him three times in my own front room and it did not come up again all night. he never mentioned it. i dont think he registered it happening.

the state of himwk 62

im going to inventory this the way i inventory a scene, because its the only way im going to get through writing it.

01
shirtless. underwear. nothing else.
no boots. this is a man who has been photographed twice and both times looked like he had been styled.
02
two large metal necklaces.
goth, heavy, chain-type. these are the only actual clothing decision in the entire outfit and he made it.
03
the hair is destroyed.
i need people to understand what that means. every single account on this website, from the caretaker to the courier to the woman at the ice cream counter, has mentioned the hair. he maintains that cut. it is the one piece of upkeep he demonstrably performs on himself. it was flat on one side and standing up on the other.
04
he had attempted eyeliner.
and it had not gone well. one side is roughly right and the other is not on the line it is supposed to be on, and both of them are smudged.
05
a bottle of 120 proof vodka, part gone.
by his own account the third one.
06
and he was wearing cologne.
im putting it last because i have thought about it more than everything above it put together. something boozy — chocolate, vanilla, rum. it is a real fragrance, applied deliberately, and it was applied recently enough to still be present under three bottles of spirits.

he could not find his shirt. he did his eyeliner.

the conversation, such as it waswk 62
transcribed from memory, immediately after. slurring preserved.
him"you knowuh… why do they… evern bother… *hic* majking… 120 prooof… i had to drink,,,, lioke… three of em… do you have,, like any wood alcohual… orso emthing"
[i want it noted that a man who has been documented drinking nothing on this website in eighteen months has now asked me for methanol.]
me"jesus christ. look at you."
him"huh… what? jesus christ is here? anyways……."
[hand on my shoulder. the smell arrives about a second before he does.]
him"hiii louuuuu *hic* long timee.,… nos eee… amirite or amiritre… heheheheh"
me"v. you are a fucking mess."
him"yeasdhh… and your still a sad fuck living in an empty house. wahtsa new, buddy? wheres wk8 at……."
[he is not wrong. that is the fastest anybody has ever summarised me and he did it with a blood alcohol level that should have killed him.]
him"yuo… checkin me out… buddy?? WEEK EIGHT! kitTTY!!! where ary you…."

and she came.

straight in, no hesitation, one meow, and jumped into his arms from a standing start while he was swaying, and he caught her without looking and without spilling anything.

i tried to say something about the last two months.

me"so, last time weve spoken, youve killed like ar—"
him"yeah, shhh shut up. ive killed alot. im speaking to wk8 right npoww *hic*"

so i sat down in my own chair and waited while a man who has killed several hundred people said whoooss sa pretty giirllll to my cat for a minute and a half.

i cleared my throat. thats the entire contribution i made to the middle section of this evening.

and then the thing from the underwearwk 62

a burp of genuinely alarming duration. another swig.

"anywyaysys… yeah… ive been killing people alot, huih? speaking of which……"

and he reached into his underwear and pulled out a detonator.

"hheheh. you thought… that was a boner.. wasnbt it?"

i did. yes.

i want to note, because somebody is going to ask and because it is the only genuinely unresolved thing from that night, that i have no idea what that device is attached to. it is a real trigger of a recognisable type. he did not explain it and i did not ask and nothing has gone off since and i check the news every morning now for a reason i did not used to have.

and then he came very close to my face and said the following, which i am reproducing exactly because sanding it down would be dishonest and because he specifically told me to log it.

"im gonan a. be ohnest… *hic*. im kinda high on crack right now too, pretty boy. i couldnt get hard even if i saw you crossdress. or if *hic* some chick threw her bra on my guitar at a show. fuuck…. i gotta do another dicky twistesrs show…"

and then he turned and addressed the camera that is not there.

"youre gonna log this anbyways…
hey gyus!! it s me!! v!
brekaign the fourth wall thru your blog!
im gonna… arrange *hic* sumthin.. when i sober up."

thats the first time he has ever spoken directly to the people reading this. in eighteen months he has defaced this site three times, signed a commenter up to a mailing list, and read every word any of you have written, and he has never once said hello to you.

he did it drunk, in his underwear, holding my cat and a detonator, and he promised you a gig.

and then he leftwk 62 · 02:40ish

"anwyays. just wanted to say hiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiii…. and nopw im gonna leave. buh-bye…… i wont drive… probalbly….. have ao go day. i left some slelping pills and cash on your counter….. i lvoe you or whatever… i know saying that drives your community mad. bye…."

i had not said a word for about four minutes at that point and i did not say one then either.

he hit the door frame going out. and the wall. and something in the hall. i counted somewhere around twenty separate impacts between my chair and the outside and he did not react to any of them.

then a car started.

then my bin went over.

then he drove away.

he drove. i want that in its own paragraph. a twenty one year old with three bottles of 120 in him and a stimulant on top got into a vehicle outside my house and drove it away and i stood in my doorway and watched him do it and did not do one single thing about it.

the counterwk 62 · 03:10

he did leave them. thats the part i keep coming back to.

01
a box of sleeping tablets.
correct type, correct dose, sealed, and the brand a doctor would actually give somebody. i have written on this website eleven times that i do not sleep. i have never once asked anybody for anything about it.
02
a quantity of cash, squared to the edge of the counter.
i want to be precise. everything about that man last night was uncoordinated. he could not get through a door. he could not finish a sentence. and the cash is square to the counter edge and the box is square to the cash.

every other faculty he has was gone. that one was not.

and the notes do not say BONER on them. i checked all of them. thirteen months of that joke and this is the first time.

what i actually cannot get pastwk 62 · 05:00

its not the crack and its not the detonator and its not the driving, although the driving is the one that is going to keep me up.

its the cologne.

at some point last night, before three bottles of vodka and whatever else, a twenty one year old stood somewhere and put on a fragrance.

you dont do that on the way to somewhere. you do it before you go. it is a thing you do when you have decided in advance that you are going to see somebody and you would like to have made an effort about it.

and then he drank enough to kill a person, and could not find a shirt, and did his eyeliner anyway, and came here, and insulted my house, and talked to the cat for ninety seconds, and told the readers of this website that hes going to put on another show, and left me something for the thing i have never asked anybody for help with.

"i lvoe you or whatever…
i know saying that drives your community mad."

hes said that once before. week twenty two, through a speaker system he had installed in my walls, at the end of a sixteen day prank, to a man he had just watched escape out of a window in a panic.

and the second half of that sentence is the part nobody is going to talk about and its the part that is actually new. i know saying that drives your community mad.

hes not saying it to me. hes saying it to you. he has read this guestbook for a year and a half and he knows exactly which four words make eight hundred people lose their minds and he deployed them, drunk, on purpose, as a bit, and the bit is that he meant it.

i did not ask him a single question.

eighteen months. the four months, the record, the photographs, the room, the boards, the money, why the ear, why lemons, why that song, what the detonator is for, where she was for nine days, what he wants from me.

he was in that chair for the better part of an hour and i asked him nothing, and i have spent all morning working out why, and the answer is that the second i ask him something its an interview.

and it wasnt one. thats the whole entry. it was the first time in a year and a half that it wasnt one.

— lou

wk 64 — 03:33

every screen in night city. i am writing this on the machine it happened to, and it is still happening while i type, and there are fifty one hours left on it.

everythingwk 64 · 03:33:00

im not going to be able to describe the scale of this properly and im going to try anyway.

every screen. not most. not a network, not a provider, not a district. my machine, my phone, the television i do not use, the boards outside, the transit displays, the plaza, the med centre intake screens, the vending units, the taxi tops, the ad panels in the lifts.

a woman in the guestbook has posted that it came up on the diagnostic display of a kitchen appliance.

and it was simultaneous. thats the part nobody can get past. not a wave, not a rollout — every one of them at 03:33:00 to the second.

people are already saying datakrash and i understand why and i think its the wrong word, and somebody in the guestbook has explained why better than i can and im going to let them.

theres a countdown in it. its live in the archive because it was live on the night and i am not going to freeze the one part of it that was the point.

the first thing he sayswk 64

"REMEMBER WHEN I WAS DRUNKER THAN SHIT ON LIKE, TWO WEEKS AGOS BLOG!! REMEMBER THE DETONATOR! GOOD THING I DO!"

hes right and i want to own it before anybody else does.

he pulled that out of his underwear in my front room, made a joke about it, and then never mentioned it again for the rest of the night. i wrote four paragraphs about the cologne and i wrote one about the detonator and in that paragraph i said i had no idea what it was attached to and that nothing had gone off.

birdie told me in the thread that in forty years she had never seen one turn out to be nothing. she was right and i logged it and moved on.

it was attached to the thing
he announced eleven days earlier
on thirty six billboards.

its in the wk 59 page. its the last paragraph. its in capitals. everybody read it, four million people discussed it, two shelters shut over it, and then it was signed P.S. MEOW and the whole city filed it as a joke.

and the reason it read as a joke is that he forgot about it himself for two weeks. he had the trigger on him and he used it as a punchline about his own crotch. he is not being clever here. he genuinely remembered.

the listwk 64

one hundred and seven facilities.

he names them. all of them, out loud, in one take, in fifty eight seconds, and he does not stumble and he does not check anything and there is no cut in the recording.

ive had it verified against three separate registries by three separate people in the guestbook overnight. its complete. its every licensed kill facility operating in this city and it includes four that are contracted rather than municipal and are not on the public list at all.

the way he says them is the thing. its not a threat delivery. its the cadence you use reading out a shopping list, and it goes on for a minute, and it is the single most frightening minute of anything he has ever done, and nothing happens in it.

ive spent eighteen months writing about a man who does research. the milkshake, the scrapbook, the wife, the son, three hundred and ninety one households means-tested against medical debt.

this is that again. its just that this time you can hear it.

the buttonwk 64

and now the part that this city is actually going to have to deal with, and it is not the bomb.

there is a dismiss button.

it is on consumer hardware. phones, home terminals, personal machines, entertainment units. it works. it worked first time, every time, for everybody who had one, and i pressed mine and it went away and it has not come back.

it is not on corporate displays. it is not on the municipal boards, the transit screens, the plaza, the ad panels, or anything registered above the small business threshold.

those have been running it on a loop for twenty one hours.

01
he did not just take every screen in the city.
he took every screen in the city, sorted them by who owns them, and gave one group an exit.
02
and the sort is accurate.
ive had about eleven hundred reports overnight and the line holds. small businesses have the button. the laundrette has the button. the shelter behind the laundrette has the button. corpo plaza does not and cannot and has been playing it since half three yesterday morning.
03
which means the capability is not the demonstration.
taking everything is the loud part. the quiet part is that he could do it selectively, by ownership, at citywide scale, and chose to show you that he could.

"AND DONT WORRY, MY FELLOW WORKING CLASS CITIZENS! YOU GUYS HAVE A BUTTON… EVERYBODY ELSE, THOUGH? CORPOS, CORPO BILLBOARDS, AND EVERY SINGLE SCUM OF THE EARTH 1%ERS! FIGURE IT OUT YOURSELF!"

ive written four hundred thousand words about this man and i have never once been able to find a politics in him. i have looked. ive been asked about it in the q&a nine times and every time i have said the same thing, which is that he does not appear to have one, that he has never made a statement about anything, and that reading one into him is the single easiest mistake available.

im not saying he has one now. im saying that at half three yesterday morning he divided this entire city into two groups, correctly, in about a second, and gave one of them a door.

and the reason for all of itwk 64 · 22:00

seventy two hours to change policy. thats the demand. thats the whole demand.

not money. not a name, not a release, not an admission, not a resignation, not access to anything. change the policies so the animals are not killed.

and there is a second demand which everybody has read as a joke and which i do not think is one:

"I NEED TO MAKE MORE TERRORISTIC THREATS! AFTER ALL, HOW ELSE WILL I GET MORE PEOPLE TO COME TO MY NEXT SLAM GIG?"

he told me hed arrange something when he sobered up. he said it in my front room, in his underwear, holding my cat, and he said it to you and not to me.

this is the promotion.

the largest cyberattack in the history of this city
is a policy demand
and a flyer.

im going to say the thing pd_marchetti already said better than i can and which nobody wanted to hear four weeks ago.

nothing is going to happen to him. it was already true before this. its more true now, because the mechanism by which anything would happen to him is currently displaying his face and cannot be turned off by the people who own it.

the working theory in this guestbook for a month has been that the realistic outcome is a job offer.

fifty one hours left.

— lou

and then it stalls. everything easy has gone. what is left has a board, a contract or a committee.
