the shape of that is the whole story and it is not a moral shape.

nothing for twelve hours, because everybody was waiting to see if anybody else went first. then three, all of them places owned by one person who had nobody to consult and nobody to hide behind.

then a stall at eleven, for about twelve hours, which is where everything that could move quickly had already moved.

and then thirty three in six hours, and by every account i have that was not a change of heart in anybody. it was the moment being on the list became more dangerous than the policy was profitable, and once four or five went the rest was arithmetic.

a hundred and four facilities changed a policy in three days that campaigners have been asking them to change for two decades. that is a real sentence and everybody in this city is going to have to live inside it.

hour thirty onewk 64 +3

im putting this on its own and above the ending because it happened first and because it is going to get buried underneath the ending, and it should not be.

her name was Rosario Amador Piña. sixty one. she volunteered at a municipal facility in santo domingo three nights a week and had done for nine years.

her facility complied at hour nineteen. it was one of the early ones. she was not defying anybody and she was not in danger from anybody.

they were moving animals out overnight because nobody had planned for what compliance actually meant in a building with two hundred animals in it and no capacity anywhere to send them, and there were four people doing it, and it had been going for eleven hours.

she collapsed at about half four in the morning. cardiac. she was pronounced at the scene.

nobody touched her. nobody threatened her. she is not on that list of a hundred and seven and neither is her building by then.

she is on the names page.

i have thought about that for a day and a half and i have had two people tell me she does not belong there because it was her heart, and i understand the argument and i am not taking it.

the page is for people who did not deserve it. she was moving cats out of a building at half four in the morning because a man put a clock on a screen, and she is dead, and if the page is not for her then i do not know what i have been doing for four months.

her family has been asked and they said yes. her daughter asked me to include that she was a volunteer and not staff, because she was proud of that.

the threewk 64 +3 · H+70

with two hours left there were three.

01 — the one that said nocorporate contracted · city center

an operator with a parent above it and a legal department, which put out a statement at hour fifty two saying it would not amend operational policy under duress and that it had confidence in law enforcement.

at hour sixty eight it emptied the building of staff. quietly, no announcement, and the statement stayed up.

at 03:33:00 the animals were not in it. every one of them — four hundred and ten by the count that has been published since — was already out, and had been for about ninety minutes, and nobody working there had moved them.

the building came down at 03:41. empty. nobody in it, nothing alive in it. the statement is still up on their site and has not been amended and i suspect it never will be.

02 — the one that could notmunicipal · watson

this is the one i have spent all day on and it is the most night city thing that has ever happened.

they wanted to comply. they voted to comply. they voted at hour forty and it passed unanimously among everybody present, and it did not carry, because the amendment required a quorum of seven and four members did not attend.

they tried again at hour fifty six. same four absent. two were out of the city, one had stopped answering, and one had, by his own later account, decided the whole thing was somebody else's problem.

a facility with a hundred and sixty animals and eleven staff was going to be destroyed because four people did not come to a meeting.

and at some point between hour sixty three and hour sixty nine, all four of them arrived at that meeting room.

none of the four will say anything. one has resigned. one has left the city. the two who are still in post have given identical statements, three sentences long, which do not describe how they got there.

what is on the record is that the vote was retaken at 02:02, that it carried seven to nothing, and that the amendment was filed at 02:22 with ninety one minutes remaining.

the building is standing. everybody in it is alive. it is the only facility of the hundred and seven where somebody had to be brought to the vote, and it is the outcome i think about the most, because he could have blown it up and it would have been consistent, and instead he did the administrative version.

03 — the one nobody was left atcontracted · santo domingo

the contractor stopped existing at about hour thirty. tygr said in the guestbook on the first day that the contracts would be worthless by morning and that the operators would try to sell and then run, and that is exactly and precisely what happened.

there was nobody to sign an amendment because there was no longer an entity to sign one. no staff, no principal, no filing, and about ninety animals in a building with the power still on and nobody coming back.

at some point on the last night, all ninety were removed.

the building is standing. it was never destroyed and as far as anybody can tell it was never going to be, and i think that is because there was nobody in it to make a point to. every one of those animals has turned up somewhere in the last two days, in ones and twos, at places with the button.

03:33:00wk 64 +3

the broadcast stopped. all of it, everywhere, at once, the same way it started.

no closing message. no gloat, no summary, no sign-off, no signature. the screens simply went back to whatever they had been doing three days earlier, mid-loop, in the middle of a word.

eight minutes later one building came down in city center and it was empty and it had been emptied by somebody who did not work there.

and thats it. thats the whole ending.

a hundred and six standing.
one down, empty.
one woman dead of a heart attack
at half four on the second night.

i have gone looking for the part where this becomes a thing i can write a paragraph about and it is not there.

a hundred and four facilities in this city will not kill an animal again and that happened in three days and nothing else was ever going to make it happen. thats true.

and a sixty one year old volunteer is dead because a clock appeared on every screen in the city, and she was on the compliant side of it, and she was doing the thing he wanted done when it killed her. thats also true.

the page has seventy three names on it now.

— lou

wk 65 — he asked me to write this one

second entry he has agreed to. the first one he agreed to because he was drunk and thought it was funny. this one he asked for, out loud, unprompted, in the middle of it, and i have thought for two days about whether asking makes it alright and i have decided it does not and i am doing it anyway because he asked.

the messagewk 65 · 21:40

my machine flashed. not a defacement, not a takeover, just text on the screen i was already looking at.

"dont shoot me this time. ill be over in 5."

and he was. five minutes, near enough exactly.

he knocked. i want that written down. in nineteen months and however many entries he has come through my window, my walls, my door, my lockscreen and my bed, and on the one occasion i knew he was coming he knocked on the front door and waited.

how he lookedwk 65

pyjama bottoms. a band shirt, and i recognised the band off the station.

no eyeliner. no boots. no necklaces. hair not done, but not destroyed either — just not done. no cologne.

i tried to open with something.

me"no fancy getup today, eh?"
him"yeah, sure, lou. whatever."
[and thats when i understood what kind of evening it was.]

ive had eleven documented interactions with this man. every single one of them, without exception, has had a bit in it. a voice, a joke, a delivery, an exit line. even the flat voice is a register — its a thing he does, its got an effect it produces, and he deploys it.

there was no bit. he could not be bothered. thats the entire difference and i noticed it in four words.

he sat on the end of my bed.

what he saidwk 65
reconstructed immediately afterwards. i have not tidied the grammar.
him"what i did last night was a positive thing. objectively. i saved multiple animals. you would agree, yes?"
[i nodded. of course i nodded.]
him"i also indirectly killed a woman. not like thats a new thing for me, ive DIRECTLY killed thousands. tens of thousands. i stopped counting at 16."
[i tried to say something here. nothing came out. that happens four more times in this entry and i am going to stop noting it.]
him"Rosario fuckin Amador Piña."
[all three names. correctly. including the second surname, which about half the reporting on this got wrong.]
him"a woman, who didnt even work for a single fuckin enny. for 9 years. who would have liked what i was doing. who complied. and died. in a way i cant fucking fix."
him"theres families in that guestlog. families of people i killed. people i killed with my own two hands. kills that, i could have not have done. kills that i could have fixed. and tried."
him"i killed a person. indirectly. for only the third time in my life. the first two were my parents."

im going to stop the transcript for one paragraph.

in a year and a half he has never once told me anything. not one fact, not one date, not one confirmation. every single thing on this website was worked out, paid for, or handed to me by somebody else. he has corrected me twice and both times it was one word.

he sat on my bed and told me the count. and then he told me about his parents, unprompted, in a sentence he did not have to say, in the middle of a different subject.

him"i know youre thinking if you should log this. i dont even care. go ahead. do it. id like you to."

thats the second time hes told me to log something.

the first was three weeks ago and he was so drunk he could not stand up and he was doing a bit for the readers.

id like you to.

and thenwk 65
him"when i killed my parents, i was upset. even if they were the ones that groomed me into what i do today. even if they are indirectly responsible for tens of thousands of innocent, and not-so-innocent lives."
him"who cares if they arent innocent, either? nobody in this FUCKING CITY IS A SAINT!"

and he stood up and put his fist through my wall.

i want to be accurate about this because it is the first time i have ever seen it and because of what it means.

he bled.

nineteen months. a shotgun to the head at contact range. three rounds from me at four feet. a hundred and ten rounds in this room forty seconds later. and the only time i have ever seen anything come out of that man was when he hit a wall in a house he bought me.

it ran down his knuckles and onto his forearm and he did not look at it and he did not mention it and it was still there when he left.

ive since had it explained to me by three separate people what force that requires, given what he is made of. the phrase one of them used was that the wall was not the thing that gave.

the part i have rewritten nine timeswk 65

im going to report this the way i report a scene. its the only way im getting through it and i am aware that is the same sentence i used about the caretaker and about the cologne and i do not have another method.

him"i tried to kill myself, when i killed my parents. i was so upset that i killed the people that made me who i was today. that i tried to kill myself. and i couldnt."
him"because i rival fucking adam smasher in levels of chrome. look. look. at this."

and then he demonstrated it.

i am not going to describe it round by round and i am not going to put the sequence in an evidence table the way i do with everything else, because i have looked at what that would produce on the page and i am not making that.

here is what i will give you, because i counted, because i always count, and because counting was the only thing i was capable of doing while it happened.

110
rounds discharged, in my bedroom, in under forty seconds.
two weapons. one emptied twice into the same place. one emptied once into everywhere else. every round of it into himself.
0
effect.
he sat back down. he was not out of breath. there was nothing to treat and nothing to look at.

my ears rang for two days. there is damage in that room i am not repairing yet.

and then, sitting on the end of my bed:

"who cares? who cares about anything?
why do i care about this fucking woman so much?"

he asked me that. out loud, as a question, to me, and he waited.

and i said nothing. again. for the fifth time that evening and the eleventh time in nineteen months.

i have four hundred and something thousand words on this website. ive built a case file, a names page, a ballistics section and seventy three answered questions. a twenty one year old sat on my bed and asked me why he cared about somebody and i did not open my mouth.

how he leftwk 65 · 22:30ish
him"im gonna drive home, and get drunker than i did last time. you wont be hearing from me for a bit."
him"the same sleeping pills are on the counter again. also got week 8 some expensive ass steak. feed her whenever."
him"bye, relay."

and he went.

two things about that and then im finishing this entry.

01
he called me relay.
he has called me lou since the night he said his own name out loud in my bedroom. every single time, without exception, for over a year. tonight he used the handle on the masthead. i do not know what that is and i have not stopped turning it over.
02
and he did not drive.
i stood in the doorway and waited for it, because last time i stood in the same doorway and watched him get into a car at a blood alcohol level that should have killed him, and did nothing, and static_hymn was right to put me on the spot about it in the thread.

no engine. nothing. he said he was going to drive and then he walked, and i listened until i could not hear him any more, and it took a while.

the pills were on the counter. correct type, correct dose, sealed.

the steak is real and it is absurd and it cost more than everything else in my fridge combined. she has had some. she liked it.

and the notes did not say BONER again. thats twice now.

what he actually asked me forwk 65 · 05:00

ive had two days and here is the only thing i have got and im putting it up plainly rather than dressing it.

he did not come here to confess and he did not come here for absolution and he certainly did not come here for me, because i said eleven words all night and four of them were a joke about his outfit.

he came here because this is the place where things get written down.

he has read this website every day for a year and a half. he knows exactly what it is. he knows about the names page and he knows i asked seventy three families for permission one at a time and he knows what teodora writes in the guestbook every single week and he has never once interfered with any of it.

and when he needed something to be true
somewhere outside his own head,
he came to the archive.

id like you to.

hes not asking me to publish. hes asking me to record it. those are different jobs and ive been doing the first one for nineteen months while telling everybody it was the second.

im not going to write the paragraph where i tell you how i feel about him. ive never written it and im not starting now and i think everybody reading this can do it themselves at this point.

what i am going to say is this, and its the first sentence on this entire website that is addressed to one person, and hes going to read it because he reads everything.

i dont know why you care about her. i dont think thats a question with an answer and i dont think you were really asking me. but you got her name right, all three of it, including the part nearly every outlet in this city got wrong, and youve never once in your life bothered to get something right that didnt matter to you.

she is on the page. she is going to stay on the page. and when you asked me to write this down, i wrote it down.

thats all i have got. come back when youre ready and dont drive.

— lou

wk 81 — the piña concert

four months of nothing. and then posters. i went. i did not take a camera and that is the first time in nineteen years i have gone anywhere without one on purpose.

sixteen weekswk 66 → wk 80

he said i would not be hearing from him for a bit and then i did not hear from him for a bit.

no visits. no objects. nothing on the desk, nothing in the fridge, nothing on any screen anywhere in this city. the station kept running and nothing was added to it. birdie heard nothing, tygr heard nothing, and the guestbook went quiet in a way it has not been since before the club.

i wrote nine entries in those sixteen weeks and eight of them were about the names page. its at ninety four now.

and then last thursday the posters went up.

THE PIÑA CONCERT
one night · doors 19:00 · free entry
an address in westbrook. a bar that has been doing the same cocktail
for thirty one years and has it painted on the window.

paper. actual paper, flyposted by hand, in about nine districts. no boards, no broadcast, no takeover, nothing hacked. somebody with a bucket of paste and a ladder.

everybody in this city worked out what it was inside about an hour, and nobody said it out loud, and about three thousand people turned up.

the roomwk 81 · 19:00

every instrument you can think of. thats not a figure of speech and i counted what i could — a full kit, four guitars, an upright bass, brass on a rack, a pipe organ that had been brought in and did not fit properly, strings, an accordion, a set of pipes, three keyboards, and a table of things i could not identify.

all of it on a stage in a bar in westbrook that normally has a jukebox.

he came out and three thousand people made a noise i have never heard indoors.

and he took the mic, and there was feedback, and he said:

"THANK YOU, THANK YOU!"

and the room went up again. and then:

"but, please, no cheering.
this isnt about me."

and three thousand people stopped.

and then he said her namewk 81 · 19:04

"this is about Rosario Amador Piña."

and then he said it again, and spelled it out, letter by letter, into a microphone, to three thousand people.

every letter. both surnames. the tilde.

im going to say why that landed the way it did for the people in that room who knew, and it is the only piece of analysis in this entire entry.

four outlets in this city reported her death. three of them dropped the Piña. one of them spelled Amador wrong. her daughter wrote to two of them and neither replied and neither corrected it, and within nine days there was nothing about her anywhere.

a man who has never explained himself once in nineteen months stood in a bar and spelled a dead volunteer's name out letter by letter so that three thousand people would have it right.

"this concert is about her. and the amazing woman she was. every drink, and every plate of food at this place, is on me."

and the room started to go up again, because thats what rooms do.

and he looked at them.

i was about forty feet back and i saw it and i am telling you that three thousand people put themselves away in under two seconds. no gesture, no raised hand, nothing said. he looked at them and the room understood that it had made this about the wrong thing, and corrected itself, and went quiet.

"thank you. every single enny spent here will be going to her family. have a good night."

have a good night. thats the whole speech. thirty eight words including her name twice.

ten hours and twelve minuteswk 81 · 19:06 → 05:18

one song. a hundred times. a hundred different ways.

Escape, by Rupert Holmes, 1979. a hundred and two years old. it is on the station and it always has been, in the block i catalogued in week seventeen, and i never once thought about it.

this is where i tell you what everybody in this city has spent four days failing to explain to people who were not there, which is that it was funny. for most of ten hours it was very funny, and it was meant to be, and he was enjoying himself enormously, and by about hour three the room had stopped being able to breathe properly.

the barbershop quartet is one man with a loop pedal and it is the single funniest thing i have ever seen a human being do.

the twenty eight minute ambient version emptied about a third of the room, which he could see, and he played all twenty eight minutes.

the hospital hold music version made a woman near me laugh so hard she had to sit on the floor.

and every drink went out free all night and the tills kept ringing anyway because people paid regardless, and the bar has confirmed the number and i am not printing it, and all of it has gone where he said it would go.

the hundredthwk 81 · 05:18

ninety nine of them were arrangements.

the hundredth is the song.

no genre. no gimmick. no joke in it anywhere. one man, an acoustic guitar, and a hundred and two year old pop song about two people who do not recognise each other, played the way it was written, at twenty past five in the morning, to about eleven hundred people who were still there.

and he did not say anything at the end of it. he put the guitar down and walked off and did not come back and there was no encore and nobody asked for one.

ninety nine jokes
and then the song.

im not going to write the paragraph explaining that. its the best-constructed thing i have ever seen anybody do and i have been in this city a long time and i am not going to stand in front of it and point.

why that songwk 81 · later

everybody worked out the surname joke instantly. thats the surface and it is the part that reads worst if you were not there.

heres the part that took me until wednesday, because somebody in the guestbook told me and i did not know it.

people made that joke to her constantly. for nine years, at the shelter, every vet and every driver and every new volunteer, the same tired gag about her surname.

and she loved it. every single time. not tolerated — loved, laughed at it properly, for nine years, and the people who knew her say it never once got old for her and that they kept doing it because of what it did to her face.

that is not something you can find out. its not in any record. its not in the four articles or the two corrections nobody made. its a thing about a person that exists only inside the small number of people who were in a room with her.

and he found it.

the same way he found the second surname. the same way he found out a boy was placed with two foster mothers. the same way he found little printed footballs for a scrapbook about somebody else's brother.

he did not make a joke about a dead woman.
he found out what made her laugh
and did ten hours of it.

— lou

the names

this page is not an entry. theres no writing on it past the rules at the top and there never will be. if youre looking for the file, its everywhere else on this website.

how this page works.
  1. names only. no methods, no site numbers, no districts, no dates, no photographs, and nothing i have written.
  2. nobody goes up without a family member asking, or without me verifying against two independent records and then asking anyway if theres anybody to ask.
  3. spellings checked twice. if i have it wrong, message me and it is fixed the same hour, and i will not ask you to prove anything.
  4. anybody can be taken down again, at any time, for any reason or none. one person has already asked and it was down in nine minutes and i did not ask why.
  5. this page will never be finished. i want that stated rather than implied.

why the board is still upwk 14 · 05:55

my sister asked me over the phone what my apartment looks like now and i lied to her. thats the entry. thats the whole entry.

questions

questions i get asked constantly

i wrote the first thirteen of these in week seventeen so i could stop typing the same six paragraphs in the replies. it was thirteen. its wk 52 now and its forty seven. i have grouped them because it got long enough that grouping it became the polite thing to do.

these are longer and more considered than anything i say in the thread, because the thread is me at 4am and this is me having thought about it. where an old answer stopped being true i have left it up with the update underneath, because thats the arrangement and it always has been.

the site · why it exists, what it is now
why is it called dead air

broadcast term. its the silence when a signal stops and nobody has said anything yet and everybody is still listening.

i picked it in week one because i thought it described him. rooms he had left. the quiet after.

ecm_null pointed out in week thirty that it is currently the least accurate title on the net, and i want to formally agree. the noisiest page on this site is a comment thread about a milkshake. the second noisiest is a name.

im not changing it. it stopped being a description a while ago and became the thing you call a place.

asked ~4,000 times
why dont you monetise this

ive been offered advertising, sponsorship, syndication, three book deals, a documentary, and a very polite letter from an outfit that wanted to sell branded merchandise of a machined casing.

no to all of it, and the reason has not changed since week sixteen: the second this has money attached its a product, and a product has an audience, and i have spent seven months finding out i am not the one with an audience here.

also, and more practically, im not short. a man left ninety four thousand eurodollars in my spare room with a joke written on them. it is the least complicated money in this city and the most complicated money in my life.

asked ~9,000 times
can i send you money / can i help

no money. genuinely, and thank you.

if you want to do something: there are people in the guestbook who occasionally need practical things that arent money — an introduction, a lift, somebody who knows a process. that has quietly become about a third of what this comment section does and it happens without me.

four people have offered me a spare room. i have taken none of them, because anybody who houses me is a person with a documented address, and thirty one people once came through a front door of mine. i read all four at four in the morning and it was not nothing.

asked ~6,000 times
can i mirror or archive the site

please dont.

not because i want control of it. because a mirror is a copy that i cannot correct, and i have corrected this site publicly about nine times, including a wording change that a woman had to ask me for about her own brother.

a frozen copy of this website is a version where that correction never happened. thats the whole objection and its enough.

asked ~2,000 times
why is there no real comment system / why cant i edit

because i bought a template for nine eddies in 2075 and i am a photographer.

the no-edits thing was an accident that i have since decided to keep. people write things here at four in the morning and mean them, and being able to quietly smooth them afterwards would change what this place is.

you can delete. deletions are yours and i dont restore them and i dont name anybody who makes one. about four hundred people deleted in one morning in week seventeen and i have never said a word about who.

asked constantly
what happens to this site if something happens to you

it stays up. its paid for a long way forward, in cash, and the arrangement does not require me to be alive to renew it.

three people have instructions and none of them know about the other two. none of them can edit anything. all any of them can do is confirm that i am not going to post again, and put that on the front page, and then leave it exactly as it is.

i want to say the actual reason, because "in case i die" sounds dramatic and its not the point. theres a name on this website that his sister typed. its the only place in this city it is written down. that is not mine to let expire.

asked ~11,000 times
him · the ones i mostly cant answer
why not go to ncpd

with what. i have photographs of rooms, a station number that isnt registered anywhere, an interview with a man whose gang wont go near him, and a story about waking up next to a limb i can no longer produce.

and thats the polite version. the real version is that ncpd closed four of these as psych episodes and one as an equipment fault while a corp risk analyst was screaming about the pattern internally until he stopped screaming permanently. they are not a party i can bring evidence to. theyre a party in the file.

asked ~200 times
why dont you just stop

i want to answer this one seriously because it deserves better than the flippant version i usually give.

stopping was available in week six. it was probably available in week nine. it stopped being available somewhere around the point that he started doing things to me on a schedule, because at that point not writing isnt neutral, its a choice he can observe me making. theres no off position. theres only me continuing or me visibly stopping, and i have no idea which one is more interesting to him and i am not willing to find out by experiment.

thats the honest structural answer. the honest personal answer is that i dont want to and i have run out of energy to pretend otherwise for the comment section.

asked ~340 times
are you in love with him

this gets asked maybe forty times a week, usually as an insult, occasionally sincerely, and once in a long message from someone who was clearly trying to help.

no. and i understand why the file reads that way and im not going to pretend its an unreasonable question when i have a section on this website titled "the subject" and i once wrote that i hoped a room would slow down for me too.

what it actually is, i think, is closer to what happens to people who study one thing for too long with nobody to talk to about it. he is the most interesting thing that has ever happened in my life and he is the worst thing that has ever happened in my life and those are the same sentence. i dont want to be near him. i want to understand him, which turns out to be a hunger that behaves almost identically from the outside and is much harder to talk yourself out of.

the kid from the service road spent eleven weeks trying to make there be a message. im doing a longer version of the same thing with better equipment.

asked constantly, in every register
is he still coming round

as of wk 31, four visits in person, one photograph, and two months of nothing before it.

i dont have a schedule. ive tried to build one twice and both times the pattern broke the following week, and i now think there isnt one and that i was doing the thing where a person finds a rhythm in weather.

the fridge is stocked. thats the whole system. i buy a tub every fortnight and it goes off and i buy another one, and about once every eight weeks something happens.

asked every single day
are you two friends

i dont know and i am not being coy.

heres what i can list. he has never asked me a question about myself. i have never had a conversation with him that lasted longer than ninety seconds. he has never been in a room for the part where i answer him. i do not know where he lives, what he does on a tuesday, or whether he sleeps.

and: he knows my legal name, my school, a man i had not thought about in fifteen years, what i would write on a piece of paper and put in a drawer, and the eating schedule of my cat. he has read every word i have written and most of what all of you have written. he has twice said a version of the same sentence and left before i could respond to it.

i genuinely cannot tell you what the word for that is. its not nothing and its not friendship as i have previously understood the term, and i have stopped needing to file it.

asked ~40,000 times
why do you keep buying the ice cream

because its a fortnightly thing i do that takes four minutes and it is the only channel that has ever demonstrably worked.

he came round and tried it once and hated it enough to spit it on my carpet. thats the entire body of evidence that anything i put in that fridge is ever read. its also more two-way traffic than i had in the first five months.

and yes. i know. everybody in this comment section knows.

asked ~15,000 times
is he a good person

[ original wk 17 answer preserved below ]

i dont think thats a question that survives contact with the evidence.

six coolers, sealed and powered and returned to families. nine men in a warehouse who all woke up. a kid on the service road who is alive and will never be alright. twenty eight or thirty one people in the same building who arent. two men on my floor. an arm on my pillow.

all of that is one person and it is all consistent with itself, which is the part that stops it being a comfortable answer in either direction.

updated wk 31: two people have now been visited by him because of something they wrote in this guestbook. one got fifty thousand eddies and the first real dairy of her life. one got two hundred photographs of her murdered brother and a sentence that took the last clean thing she had.

i am not updating the answer. i am adding the two hardest data points i have and leaving the answer exactly where it was, because they dont move it, and thats the finding.

asked ~90,000 times
does he actually mean it

i have two instances. wk 22, played off a speaker system by a cat after four lines of screaming, scripted in advance. wk 31, in red marker on a printed photograph, shortened, with nothing in front of it.

both times he was somewhere else by the time i read it.

i cannot eliminate either reading and i have stopped trying, and i want to be clear that stopping is not the same as deciding. its just that i spent four days on a tub of ice cream once and the answer turned out to be that he likes cookies and cream, and i learned something permanent from that.

k_tanaka said the short version usually means it was true the first time. thats the best thing anybody has offered me on it and im not going to improve on it, so im putting it here instead of an answer.

asked ~200,000 times since wk 22
is johnny silverhand alive

i dont know. i have one photograph, i have covered the only part of it worth anything, and i am not going to build four thousand words on an object again.

what i have is in the wk 31 entry, all four points, and i am not adding a fifth in a q&a.

what i will say, because people keep asking me to speculate and i keep refusing and it looks like evasion: the week six slug is the part i cant put down. that was logged before he knew i existed. everything else about him could be a joke he built. that couldnt, because there was nobody to build it for.

the single most asked question in the history of this website, in nine days
why wont you publish the photograph

ive published the photograph. what i havent published is his face, and thats a different sentence.

a written description put three offers in private channels inside four hours in week twenty one, and one of them was not money. thats a description. this is a face.

and the second reason, which i put in the entry and which matters more: it wouldnt even work. hes presented three completely different ways in front of me. a face in one photograph does not tell you what walks into a room on a friday. so publishing it would be the largest thing i own, given away, to prove i had it.

asked ~120,000 times in nine days
whats the deal with 3:33

3_33 told me in week seventeen it was a doorbell and not a message. an optic package has a sleep cycle process, it can be poked, you would not feel it, you would just be awake.

i accepted that and crossed it off the board.

then in wk 20 my eyes went to a clock and he took my head in his hand and turned it back, and broke a joke he was enjoying to do it.

so: its a doorbell, and he picked the tune, and he does not want me looking at it, and i have put it back on the board and i am not asking again. thats the complete state of it and i expect it to stay there.

asked ~30,000 times
what do you actually think he wants

after seventeen weeks: to be recorded accurately, by someone competent, without being asked to explain himself.

thats it. thats the whole theory and its taken me four months to get to something that boring.

he doesnt want a witness, he had witnesses, they all say the same three words and none of them can describe him. he wanted a file. he found a man who makes files for a living and who was already, accidentally, making his.

asked ~110 times
is he a good person

i dont think thats a question that survives contact with the evidence.

six coolers, sealed and powered and returned to families. nine men in a warehouse who all woke up. a kid on the service road who is alive and will never be alright. twenty eight or thirty one people in the same building who arent. two men on my floor. an arm on my pillow.

all of that is one person and it is all consistent with itself, which is the part that stops it being a comfortable answer in either direction. hes not a monster who occasionally slips and does something kind and hes not a hero with a body count he regrets. hes something with rules, and the rules are consistent, and i have no idea what they are, and every time i think ive got one it turns out to be a coincidence in a small sample.

asked ~90 times
me · the ones i answer badly
what do you do for work now

scenes. same as before. four in week twenty four, more since, for a fixer who has never once mentioned him to me and who i suspect is being deliberate about it.

im slower than i was and my sightlines are worse because i stop down now, which sixteen_frames told me to do in week ten and which i finally did in week eleven. the floor detail is better. everything else takes longer.

i am, on any objective measure, a worse nightcrawler than i was in february and a considerably better photographer.

asked ~7,000 times
have you met any of us

a few. 35mm_gordon in week twenty seven, six hours in a booth, no camera. thats the only one i am going to name because he named it himself first.

i have not met nia and i have not met teodora and i am not going to unless they ask, in that order, and neither has, and both of them have my whole attention if they ever do.

doc_wisp i have never met and never will, and thats his rule, and its the correct rule, and it is the reason i actually listen to him.

asked ~5,000 times
are you still going

yes. mondays and thursdays since week twenty five. it used to be tuesdays and it used to be one.

im not going to write about what gets said in there. that is the one file that stays shut and it is the only thing on this website i have never once been tempted to publish, which after seven months of publishing everything is information about how much it matters.

asked ~20,000 times
do you ever get scared anymore

not of him. i want to be careful with that sentence because it sounds like bravado and it isnt, its an evidence-based position: he has had about nine unambiguous opportunities and used none of them, and the one time somebody else took an opportunity he removed them from my floor.

what i get instead is worse and harder to describe. i get a thing where i cannot tell if a week was real. i checked a painted-shut window eleven times in one day in week twenty two and it was not because i thought it had moved.

that is the actual damage. its not fear. its that somebody built me a city once and now i have to take the ordinary one on faith.

asked ~14,000 times
what happened to the spoon / the wreath / the description

the spoon was handled twenty minutes after dust_off told me what it was, and i am not saying how, and it is not in this house.

the wreath is not in this house either. it went somewhere the same week hollis told me what it was worth. i have not looked at it since and i have thought about looking at it approximately every day.

the description is in a file that is not on this machine and not at this address and has not been opened since i wrote it. 3_33 voted destroy rather than no, on the grounds that i have a documented four month history of being unable to leave a thing alone.

theyre right and i havent done it. thats the honest state of that one and it has been the honest state of it for ten weeks.

asked ~25,000 times
do you regret publishing case eighteen

this is the one i get asked in the most different tones and i have never given the same answer twice, so heres the one i actually hold.

no, and i would do it again, and it cost more than i thought and most of the cost landed on other people.

sixty two words with no names in them. a plate came off a car in ninety nine minutes and a man was in my front room by morning saying my legal name in a voice with nothing in it. regina sat on that folder for six years and told me exactly what would happen and she was right about all of it.

and i am still a nightcrawler. at some point declining to write down a true thing because the subject was kind to you is the moment you become a man keeping a diary about his friend.

both of those. permanently. i have stopped waiting for one of them to win.

asked ~60,000 times
what would you do if he never came back

i had eight weeks of it in wk 24 through 31 and i want to report honestly on them because everybody assumed it would break me.

they were the best eight weeks since february. i worked, i slept, i went out, i got a scan, i sat in a booth for six hours without a camera. for about five of those weeks i stopped listening for the door.

and i bought a tub of ice cream every fortnight the entire time and threw the old one out.

so: id be fine, and id keep the fridge stocked, and both of those are true and i have stopped finding it embarrassing.

asked ~35,000 times
how do you afford any of this

i dont. i am four months behind. i have sold almost nothing since week ten because the work i do requires me to be unremarkable and i havent been unremarkable since a hypercar was parked outside my building.

people have offered money. a lot of people, and some of it substantial, and one of them twice. im not taking it and its not pride, its that the second i take money for this it becomes a thing i produce rather than a thing that is happening to me, and the only leverage i have left is being able to say honestly that i am not doing this for anybody.

asked ~70 times
whats your real name

no. hes got it. thats already one more entity than i am comfortable with.

updated wk 20 +4: lou bloom. he said it out loud in my front room and the only protection it ever had was that he was the only one who knew. so theres no point in the answer above anymore and im leaving it up so you can see what it cost to change it.

asked ~500 times, which is its own answer about people
can you put me in touch with him

i have no way to contact him. none. not a number, not a drop, not a handle, not a frequency i can transmit on. the traffic goes exactly one direction and it always has.

two men came to my apartment believing otherwise. i want that to be the last time anybody tests it.

asked constantly and i have started deleting them
do you think youre going to die

not on friday, no. if he wanted that there were four cleaner opportunities and one of them involved him standing in my bedroom while i slept.

after friday i genuinely dont know, and not because i think hell change his mind. because i dont know what im going to be like once i have met him, and i have watched what happened to one other person who was made to look at him properly, and that man is having his arms closed up and isnt replacing the chrome.

asked ~150 times
why wont you name the man from school

because naming him makes him searchable, and because the last time i put something on this website a man went missing three days later, and because he has people who are entitled to find out what happened to him in a way that isnt reading about it on a horror blog.

and because i spent fifteen years learning not to say it. that reason is smaller than the others and its the true one.

asked ~60 times
is any of this real

i have the same answer i had in week two, which is that i have no way to prove it to you and im not going to try.

i will say the thing that convinced me, for whatever its worth. if i were inventing this i would have made him say something. anything. a line, a threat, a philosophy. every fabricated version of this story has a villain who explains himself in the third act because thats what a person writing a story would do.

hes never said a word to me. seventeen weeks. i couldnt have written that and neither could anyone else, because its not satisfying, and everything about how this has gone has been deeply unsatisfying in a way that keeps turning out to be the point.

asked ~400 times
the room · about the people in here
is nia okay / is her sister okay

treatment started in week twenty six. clean intake, nothing flagged, because doc_wisp and birdie between them made fifty thousand untraceable eurodollars boring on paper inside about a fortnight.

thats all im saying and its all shes said, and if you want more you can go and read her own comment, which is the most read thing on this site again and which i had nothing to do with, again.

asked ~50,000 times
is teodora okay

i dont know and it isnt mine to report.

she finished the book in week twenty eight and said so in about forty words and then didnt post for a fortnight, and i think that was exactly the right amount to say, and i am not going to add to it here.

what i will say, because people keep asking me to intercede: dont message her about him. several hundred of you have. she has said once that she is not a warning and not an implication and not somebody's evidence row, and that was to me, and i deserved it.

asked ~40,000 times
is it safe to post here

i have to answer this properly rather than reassuringly.

he reads the comments. not the entries, the comments, individually, by handle, and he has acted on three of them in the street or in somebody's flat. the notice above the thread has said so since week seventeen and it is not decoration.

nobody who has posted here has come to harm from him. that is a true statement and it is also nine months of sample and one person deciding, privately, using criteria none of us can see. static_hymn has said that better than me about four times.

so: post like hes reading it. hes reading it.

asked ~80,000 times
will you ever close the guestbook

no.

i thought about it for about an hour in week seventeen and then teodora told me to leave hers up and i understood that closing it would be me deciding for everybody in a room i did not build alone.

the two most read pages on this website are things i did not write. i keep the lights on. thats the job now and it took me five months to work out it was the job.

asked ~10,000 times
what happened to the cat

i genuinely did not expect this to be in the top ten and it has been for six weeks.

i dont know. she stopped being on the landing around week eight, which is when i stopped being home at hours a cat keeps. she wasnt mine and she had no name and i fed her about four nights out of seven for two years.

eleven separate people have offered to look for her. someone made a poster. i want whoever did that to know it undid me a bit and i havent been able to say so until now.

updated wk 17 +6: shes back. shes on the step. her leg is fixed and there are optics in her head and i have written a whole entry about it that you should read instead of this answer. she is, apparently, called wk8 now.

asked ~130 times, which i think says something nice about people
are you okay

no.

i want to give a fuller answer than that because a lot of the people asking are asking sincerely, and the sincere ones deserve better than a single syllable.

i sleep in daylight. i eat when i notice. i have not had a conversation with a person about anything other than this since sometime in week eleven and the last one before that was with my sister and i lied to her about my apartment. i document things compulsively now, including things that dont need it, including this. when two men broke my door down my first instinct was to reach for a camera, and when a man's head came apart four feet from my face i was already composing.

im not in danger from him. ive worked that out. im in danger from what im turning into while i wait to be told more, and thats not a thing anybody can intervene on, including the eleven of you who have offered.

five days.

asked more than anything else on this list

updated wk 31: yes, mostly, and i want that recorded with the same weight as the original.

i sleep at night more often than not. i eat when it occurs to me and thats an improvement on eating when i notice. i have had conversations with three people this quarter about things that were not him. mondays and thursdays. the scan came back unremarkable six times.

i still document compulsively. i photographed a spit stain on a carpet and put a scale reference next to it. that has not gone anywhere and i have stopped expecting it to, and doc_wisp has told me twice now that the instrument is not the problem and that something being underneath it was always the good news.

the answer in week seventeen was no. its this now. i havent deleted that one and im not going to.

updated wk 58: no.

im putting that at the top on its own line because the wk 31 update has a lot of qualifying in it and this one does not need any.

im sleeping about four hours. im eating when somebody in the guestbook reminds me, which is happening more than it used to and which i have not asked anybody to do. i am going twice a week and i went the day after and i will be going the day after this goes up.

i captioned an hour and fifty three minutes of a man dying. i did it because it was the accurate thing to do and i still think that and i would do it again and it has cost something i have not finished paying.

im alright in the sense that i am working, and the work is a page with seventy two names on it that needs to be three hundred and ninety one, and there is nobody else making it.

and the honest last line: the cat is asleep on the good chair about four feet from me and i have checked that she is still there eleven times while writing this answer.

year one · added wk 52
its been a year. whats actually changed

me, mostly. the file has got bigger and the subject has not moved an inch.

week one i was a man with a camera who could not sleep. i had an apartment with a broken stairwell, a cat i fed four nights out of seven, and a theory that three scenes were connected.

now i own a house i did not buy, i have a car i cannot drive without being seen, i have three hundred thousand people who would notice if i stopped posting, and the two most read pages on this site were written by a woman who stocks a supermarket and a woman whose brother is in a disputed number.

and i still cannot tell you where he sleeps.

asked ~90,000 times this week
is it really his birthday

i have three readings, i published all three, and i cannot eliminate any of them. thats in the wk 52 entry and im not going to re-run it here.

what i will add, because people keep asking me which one i believe rather than which one i can prove: i think it is genuinely his, and i think the fact that i started this file on it is genuinely an accident, and i think he found that funny enough to hold for eleven and a half months.

i believe that and i cannot demonstrate one word of it. thats the difference between this answer and every other answer on this page and im flagging it rather than hiding it.

asked ~400,000 times in two days
whats the list

the names from the twelfth. all hundred and three addresses, everybody i can establish, with whatever is confirmed and nothing that isnt.

its not an entry and it never will be. no methods, no photographs, no analysis, no tags, and it will never appear in a post about him. its its own page and its going to stay that way after this site stops being about anything else.

it is going slowly, because a name is not a name until somebody who knew them says it is, and about a third of them have nobody left to ask.

chidi is first. hes first because his aunt posted him first and thats the only ordering principle it has.

asked ~200,000 times
has anybody from the twelfth contacted you

yes. a lot. more than i can answer properly and i am answering all of them badly rather than answering some of them well, which i have decided is the right way round.

most of them want to know something specific and small — which room, what time, whether it was quick. i answer what i can and i say i dont know when i dont, and i have stopped softening it because the softening was for me.

four of them have asked me whether he suffered. i have told all four the truth, which is that i was not there and cannot know, and that at the address in question it would have been fast. that is true at most of them. it is not true at all of them and i am not going to lie in either direction.

asked ~50,000 times
do you think hes going to stop

no.

hes twenty one. hes been doing this since he was fourteen and the only thing that has ever changed is the scale. theres nobody who can make him stop and nothing that has to happen to him and he has never once given any indication that he wants to.

a year ago i would have written four paragraphs speculating about what would end it. i have watched every single one of my predictions about this man be wrong and i have stopped making them.

asked ~120,000 times
whats the one thing you still want to know

the four months.

regina has seventeen files of people who crossed the line and did not come back, and an eighteenth of a fourteen year old who did. and there is a gap in it, about four months long, between the eleven months of no rules and the man who turned up afterwards with contracts and targets and survivors and rules.

nobody knows what happened in there. not regina, who spent six years on it. not him, or at least not in any form he has ever indicated.

everything else on this website — the chrome, the archive, the casings, the photographs, the hundred and three — is downstream of whatever happened in those four months. it is the only load bearing thing i have never got near.

and im not going to. i went backwards once and it cost me a plate off a car and a man in my front room with nothing in his voice, and that was for sixty two words about a childhood. this would be for the thing underneath it.

asked ~30,000 times
what do you want

nobody asked me this for eleven months and then about six hundred people asked it in one week and i have not had a good answer ready, so this is me writing one for the first time.

i used to want to know what he was. i know what he is. that answer arrived in a kitchen with a spoon in it and it was not satisfying and it was correct.

i think what i want now is for the list to be finished. not for it to mean anything, not for it to do anything, just for it to be complete and accurate and somewhere permanent.

and then, honestly, i think id like to take a photograph of something that isnt a room.

new
are you okay — year one

third version of this answer. week seventeen was "no." week thirty one was "yes, mostly."

this one is: i dont know, and thats an improvement on both, because it means im actually checking rather than reporting.

i have been to a hundred and three addresses in nine days and then written a comic entry about a mans font choices a fortnight later, and both of those were me, on the same website, in the same month.

mondays and thursdays. its been a year of those too, and thats the only streak on this website i am actually proud of.

i eat. i sleep at night more often than not. there is a cat asleep on the good chair and a woman in this guestbook whose sister finished her third round on tuesday and a name at the top of a list that is not going anywhere.

im not fine. im occupied, which for a man like me has always been the nearer thing.

asked more than anything else, every week, for a year
year one, continued · everything since wk 22
are you publishing the names from the 103

yes. its started, its going to take months, and its not going to be an entry.

it will be a page with names on it and nothing else. no methods, no site numbers, no photographs, no analysis, and none of my writing anywhere near it. i have thought about that constraint for a fortnight and it is the only version i can build that isnt about me.

im working from public intake records, three coroners' techs who are helping for nothing, and families who contact me. i verify spellings twice and i ask before anybody goes up. one person has asked me to take a name down again after seeing it and it was down in nine minutes.

if somebody you know is in the 103 and you want them on it, or you want them kept off it, message me. both are equally fine and i will not ask you why.

the only question that matters now
are you going to that street from the second photograph

i said in week thirty three that i wasnt going yet, and that i was writing it down so there was a record of me knowing better first.

i still havent gone. its been nineteen weeks.

and the honest reason is not restraint. its that a fortnight after i wrote that, a hundred and three addresses happened, and i have been doing something that actually matters since, and the street has stopped being the most important thing on my desk.

birdie's offer to come with me is still open. she has never withdrawn it and she has never once chased me about it either, which is the single most professional thing anybody has done for me all year.

asked ~90,000 times
did you listen to the song

about forty times the first day and not at all since.

im not going to transcribe it, im not going to analyse it, and im not going to name what i think it means. thats the second time in a month ive been handed a piece of music and declined to take it apart and its going to be the rule from here.

what i will say is that the first minute is a grown man doing engine noises with total commitment and no irony whatsoever, and that i understood him better in that sixty seconds than in nine of the twelve months preceding it.

asked ~250,000 times in four days
is it really his birthday

i have three readings, i cannot eliminate any of them, and theyre all in the wk 52 entry.

the one i think is true is that its genuinely his, the overlap with entry 000 is a coincidence, and he found it funny enough to hold for eleven and a half months.

the one i cannot stop looking at is that its not his, and he read the date off the front page of this website, and decided it was.

im not going to try and settle it. i have never once settled anything about him by trying.

asked ~400,000 times in four days
how do you feel about him now, after the 103

this is the question and everybody asking it wants a shorter answer than i have.

i cannot hold the two halves at the same time. thats the honest report. i can hold either one for as long as you like and i cannot get them into the same sentence.

i can sit with three hundred and ninety one people and eleven sites counted by clothing. i can sit with a man building a bad audio player at half three in the morning for one listener. what i cannot do is put them next to each other and have the result be a person.

a year ago i would have called that a failure of analysis. i now think its just what its like, and that everybody in the guestbook is doing the same thing, and that the ones who claim otherwise have picked a half.

asked more than anything else since wk 51
whats the site for now

a year ago: a man taking notes so he could sleep.

six months ago: a file on a person, and i was fairly proud of it, and it was the most dangerous object in this city for a while.

now: a room where about fifty people talk honestly, a q&a i update when the truth changes, and a list of names that will take months and that nobody else is making.

the two most read pages here were not written by me. i keep the lights on. that took me five months to work out and about nine to stop resenting.

she was being sentimental. shes a ripperdoc with seventeen years in the chair and thats the only vocabulary available to her.

so: yes, probably, and probably sooner than twenty one is supposed to mean. and no, not from anything in this city, because this city has spent a year finding out it cannot.

doc_wisp said in week twenty one that the cost of running a stack like that is not paid at the time. thats the answer and its been the answer since week twenty one and everybody keeps asking me instead of reading it.

asked ~30,000 times
wk 58 · the fifty one hours
why did you archive it at all

because it was on thirty six billboards, on the plaza screen, and on broadcast, and there was nothing left for me to protect by staying out of it.

every other time i have withheld something on this website i had the only copy. that is the entire principle and it has never once been about squeamishness. withholding a thing i am the sole holder of means it does not exist. withholding a thing four million people have already watched means i have made a decision about my own comfort and called it ethics.

and there was a second reason which i put in the entry and which turned out to be the right one: inside a week there were nine competing accounts of what happened in there and most of them were wrong, and several of them were worse than what actually happened, and two of them had things in them that were invented.

the archive is the boring version. thats its whole value.

asked ~300,000 times
why wont you host the video

because a url on a billboard is a url on a billboard, and a man's face while that is happening to him is that man's face.

the billboards were public. he was not. he did not choose to be on television and he could not consent to it and he is dead and cannot be asked now.

and i want to be honest about the second half, because there is one. i have watched it. all of it, more than once, because i was captioning it. the reason i am not hosting it is not only principle. it is also that i know exactly what it does to a person to have seen it and i am not going to be the one who hands that to somebody who has not.

it exists. i have it. it is not on this machine and it is not at this address and nobody is getting it, and that includes people who think they have a good reason.

asked ~450,000 times
what was in the four minutes you cut

no.

i left the timestamps visible on both sides deliberately so you can measure the gap rather than wonder about it. it is four minutes and ten seconds. that is all the information about it that anybody is getting from me.

and i left the third archive completely uncut, with a note saying so, precisely so that the cut in the second one reads as a decision and not as a habit.

asked constantly
where did the donation money go

every route i had ran out inside four days. no processor anybody recognises, no recipient, no receipts, and the two people i asked who actually understand that side of things both came back with the same answer, which is that whatever that was, it was not built the way payment systems are built.

what i can tell you is the number moved a great deal and kept moving during the nine hours after he was dead, which is the single most upsetting fact in this entire q&a and i have thought about it more than anything except the ninety seconds.

asked ~150,000 times
do you know where she was for nine days

no, and im not investigating it, and at this point that sentence is basically a running joke on this website except that i mean it more every time.

she was fed on a schedule. she was warm. her coat is in better condition than when she left and she is not thin, and she was not frightened of anything when she came back, including the front door.

whoever had her for those nine days looked after her properly. that is the entire extent of what i know and i have decided it is the entire extent of what i want.

asked ~70,000 times
do you feel responsible

for the door, no. somebody kicked it in.

for what happened afterwards, i have gone round this for a fortnight and heres where i am.

a man broke into a house and took an animal because that animal was worth something to somebody, and the reason it was worth something to somebody is on this website, in public, with photographs, for fourteen months.

i put her on here. i wrote about the step and the feeder and the leg and the optics. i answered a q&a about her. i have made her, without ever once thinking about it, the single most publicly documented cat in this city.

i dont think that means i killed him. i think it means somebody read my website and worked out what to take, and that is a sentence i am going to be carrying for a while.

and there is a version of this where he took her because of the site and a version where he took her because she was there, and there is no way to find out now, because the only person who could tell me is dead and the person who killed him does not answer questions.

the one i get asked most since wk 58
did he build that site from yours

somebody in the guestbook has now said this to me three separate times and on the third one i stopped arguing, so ill put it here properly.

the camera did not work for the first hour. the counter is a number. the donate buttons do something nobody can trace. the only element on that entire page that functioned correctly from the first minute to the last was a chat, and he has been reading one of those daily for a year and a half.

the reading is that he did not build a broadcast, because a broadcast does not need a chat. he built a room where strangers watch a person and talk about it while it happens.

i am not going to confirm that reading because i cannot, and i am not going to reject it either, because i have read it eleven times and i have never once been able to put a hole in it.

what i will say is that if it is true, then it is the most expensive piece of criticism anybody has ever made of anything, and a man paid for it, and i did not.

asked ~180,000 times
will he do it again

i have no idea and anybody telling you they do is guessing.

what i can give you is the pattern as documented, which is that he has never repeated a format. not one. the club, the arm, the wall, the money, the robot, the wreath, the milkshake, the scrapbook, the car park, the billboards. eighteen months and every single thing he has done has been a new shape.

so on the evidence, no, not like that. which is not remotely the same as reassuring.

asked ~120,000 times
what did ncpd say

a statement went out eleven hours after the site went down. it is four paragraphs and i have read it about thirty times.

it does not name him. it does not name the victim. it does not use the word torture, or the word broadcast, or the word billboard. it refers to "material circulated online" and to "an ongoing matter" and it asks the public not to speculate.

somebody who would know told me in the guestbook that they started writing it before the second archive went up, while it was still going, and i believe them.

thats the whole institutional response to four million people watching a man die over three days on advertised infrastructure. four paragraphs, and a request that we all stop talking about it.

asked ~80,000 times

heres the update. i am not frightened of him, still, on the same evidence as before, which is nine unambiguous opportunities and none taken. what i have now that i did not have before is a very clear picture of what happens to somebody he decides about, and i have watched fifty one hours of it, and i cannot get it out of my head, and it does not feel like it is about me and it has changed the temperature of every room in this house anyway.

thats not fear. i dont have the word. its closer to how you feel about a road you know somebody died on.

asked ~30,000 times
can i download the archives / mirror them

no, and this is the one place where i have changed my mind about mirroring and im going to explain the change rather than just announce it.

ive said for a year that mirrors are frozen copies i cannot correct, and that this matters because i have corrected this website publicly about nine times including a wording change a woman had to ask me for about her own brother.

that argument is stronger here, not weaker. the archives are the version i am prepared to stand behind today. if i learn something in a month that means the second one needs a note on it, i want to be able to put the note on it.

a mirror of a torture archive is a thing that exists forever in the state somebody grabbed it in. no.

asked ~25,000 times
how are you supposed to feel about him now

im not going to tell anybody how to feel about him. i have never done that on this website and im not starting on the worst possible week to start.

what i will do is the thing i actually do, which is put the facts next to each other and leave them there.

fifty one hours. a man who poisoned his wife and put a five year old with cancer onto the street. two hundred photographs of somebody's brother in the right order with little printed footballs on the pages. six coolers he went around. three hundred and ninety one people in one night. a milkshake at six in the morning for a woman who had never had real dairy. a scrapbook. an ear. ninety seconds of holding a cat and then asking her to leave the room.

all of that is one person, at one setting, doing the complete version of whatever was in front of him. i established that in week twenty one and i have never once had to revise it and it survived this month too.

i cannot hold the two halves at the same time. i said that in week fifty two and it was true then and its more true now, and i have stopped treating it as a failure of analysis. i think its just what its like. i think everybody in that guestbook is doing the same thing and the ones who claim otherwise have picked a half.

the actual question, asked in about nine hundred different ways
not answering · asked constantly, listed for completeness
the ones i wont do

where he is. i dont know. i have never known. there has never been a return channel except a fridge.

how to reach him. i dont have one. two men tested that in my apartment in week seventeen and it went badly for them and i am not going to be the reason anybody tests it again.

the folder, the description, the wreath, or the original photograph. not for money, not for a cause, not for a story, not for somebody who has convinced themselves theyre owed it. ive had offers in all four categories and one of them was not money.

what happened at the service road, beyond what is already in the logs. theres a sister in this guestbook. go and read what she wrote instead and then think about whether you needed a number.

my address. he knows it. thats one more entity than i am comfortable with and i see no reason to make it two.

a photograph of the cat. absolutely not. this is the only one on the list im smiling about.

the video from wk 58. not for money, not for a cause, not for research, not for a documentary, and not for somebody who has convinced themselves they are owed it. i have had all five and one of them offered a great deal.

what record was playing during the 103. i could work it out in a night. im not going to, and the reason is in the wk 51 entry, and it is the only thing on this website i have ever declined to investigate on his behalf rather than mine.

all of the above, daily, forever

I woke up at 3:33. I know because I looked, and I looked because I have read this website for four months and I know what that number is here.

My desk lamp was on. I did not leave it on.

There is a scrapbook on my desk. Somebody made it by hand. It is not printed, it is assembled, the pages are laid out and the corners are done properly with those little photo corners you have to buy separately.

It is every photograph of my brother that exists.

I need to explain what that sentence means. Our mother died four years ago and I went through everything she had and I have a folder with forty one pictures in it and I have believed for four years that forty one is all there is.

There are over two hundred in the book.

Photographs from people I have never met. From his stall, from before the stall, from a job he had at seventeen that lasted five weeks. Two from a girl I did not know existed. One of him at a party I was not invited to, laughing at something out of frame, in a shirt I remember and had forgotten I remembered.

The earliest one has both of us in it. We are seven and nine and we are at the park by the water and I am pulling his ear.

The last one is from three weeks before he died. He is standing at the stall. He looks tired. He looks fine. He looks like a man having a Tuesday.

They are in order. Somebody put two hundred photographs of a person in chronological order and that means somebody worked out the order, which means somebody looked at all of them for a long time.

And there are little cut out pictures around them. Cheap clipart. Footballs, because he liked football and was terrible at it. Little cartoon dogs on the page with the dog we had. A tiny printed guitar on a page from when he was fifteen and had a guitar for a year and never learned it.

It is the corniest thing I have ever seen in my life. It is exactly the sort of thing you would do if you had never made one before and had looked up how.

teodora_mwk 23 +2 · 05:50

There was also a toy on the desk.

A plastic dinosaur. A T rex. Cheap, the kind that comes in a bag of six, the kind with the seam up the side.

When I was eleven I broke his. I broke it on purpose in an argument about something I could not tell you now, and I remember the exact face he made, and I have thought about it perhaps three times in twenty years and never for very long.

I have never told anybody that. There is nobody left who was in the room.

I turned it over.

BELONGS TO
ELÍAS
underside of the left foot

His name is Elías.

I have posted on this website since week sixteen and I have written "my brother" every single time and I have never once typed his name, and I did not decide that, I just never did it.

Somebody wrote it on the bottom of a toy in marker and put it on my desk and now it is on this page.

And the handwriting is not his. I want to say that because I looked, immediately, before anything else, and it is not his handwriting and it is not close to his handwriting. Whoever wrote it did not try.

I have read enough of this site to know what that means. That man replicates things exactly. He matched a screw. He rebuilt a computer with the right dent in it.

He could have copied it. He did not copy it. He wrote it in his own hand like a person writing a label, and I have been sitting with that since half five this morning, because I think it is the only honest thing anybody has done about my brother in a year.
