doc_wispwk 55 · 04:10

I am going to write this once, in order, while it is accurate, and then I am going to stop and I am not going to answer questions about it.

I was at my desk. Not at the practice. At home, at my own desk, at approximately half past three this morning, doing paperwork because I do not sleep well and have not for some years.

There was a person standing behind me.

I did not hear him arrive and I do not know for how long. I became aware of him the way you become aware of a change in air pressure. I did not turn around immediately. I want to record that, because it is the only decision I made in the entire episode and I do not know why I made it.

When I did turn around he was already looking at me and had been.

doc_wispwk 55 · 04:14

He did not speak. At any point. I want that established because I have read a year of accounts on this website and I understand that it is unusual.

He produced a handgun. Large frame, long barrel, and I recognised it, because I have read the arsenal section of this website approximately forty times.

He then, in the following order, and with what I can only describe as no ceremony whatsoever:

discharged one round through his own left knee.
discharged one round through his own right knee.
placed the weapon under his own chin and discharged one round through his own head.

He remained standing throughout. He did not brace against anything. Between the second and third he adjusted his grip.

doc_wispwk 55 · 04:21

Clinical observations, because they are the only thing I have and because writing them is currently the only activity available to me.

Report: Three discharges at contact range from a large-calibre weapon. In my office, which is a small room, and the acoustic event alone should have been incapacitating for both of us.

Kinetics: He was not moved. A round of that class delivers enough energy to displace a standing adult and he absorbed three and his stance did not change. There is a wall behind where he stood and it is intact.

Blood loss: Minimal and I am not able to characterise it further. There is material on my floor. It is not the volume that those three wounds produce. It is not close to that volume.

Ambulation: He walked out. Not limped. Walked, at an ordinary pace, and used the door, and closed it behind him.

Duration: From my turning around to the door closing I estimate under twenty seconds.

I have been in this profession twenty six years. I have seen a great many things that should not have been survivable and I have seen people survive some of them. I have never seen anything that did not require the person to be repaired afterwards.

doc_wispwk 55 · 05:40

I have spent an hour and I understand what it was.

It was not a threat. Nothing was demanded of me and nothing was taken. He did not touch anything in my home and he did not look at anything except me.

In week twenty one I wrote on this website that a mitigation stack of that scale does not prevent damage, it redistributes it, and that the energy still enters the body, and that the cost is not paid at the time but later, and in tissue.

In week fifty four I wrote that I would not speculate further about somebody who was not my patient.

He has read both of those. He has read everything I have written here for a year, which I have known since the mailing list and have never quite believed.

This morning he came to my house and presented me with data.

That is what it was. He did not argue with me and he could not have, because he has never in his life explained anything to anybody. So he did the only thing available, which was to walk into a clinician's home at half three in the morning and run the experiment in front of him.

doc_wispwk 55 · 06:15

And it does not work.

I have had two hours now and I want this on the record with the same weight as everything above it.

He disproved a claim I did not make.

I never said he would die tonight. I never said he could be shot. I said that absorbing that quantity of energy has a cost that is deferred, and that deferred costs are paid, and that nobody who accumulates one comes in for a check-up — they come in once.

Three rounds at contact range and walking out unassisted disproves none of that. It is, in fact, the most emphatic possible demonstration of it. He has just voluntarily added three of the largest deferrals of his life to an account he has never once looked at, in order to make a point to a man he has never met.

And here is the observation I would make if he were my patient, which he is not, and which I am making anyway because he is going to read it.

A person who genuinely believed he was fine would not need to demonstrate it at four in the morning to a stranger who cannot do anything about it either way.

That is all. I am not going to post about this again.

doc_wispwk 58 +1

The laugh.

Lou has written it accurately and has rewritten it six times, which is the correct number, because it is the single most difficult observation in this entire archive.

It is not the four seconds from the previous night. That was something I would have called predatory and would have been comfortable calling that.

This is a normal laugh. It is the laugh of a person who has amused himself and cannot stop. It has breath in it. It has a recovery in it.

I told this comment section last week that I no longer believe there is an underneath, and that I think there are several states and none of them is the real one. I want to revise that in one direction only.

That laugh is not a state he switched into. Everything else last night was constructed — the wait, the ear, the greeting, the joke. That was not. For twenty two seconds he was simply enjoying something, in the ordinary way, and what he was enjoying was a lie he had made up thirty seconds earlier.

wk 81 — the piña concert
m_pinawk 81 · 06:40

I was there.

Nobody knew. I did not tell Mr Bloom and I did not tell anybody here and I stood at the back near the door for ten hours and twelve minutes and I did not speak to one person.

I went because I was angry. I want to start there because I am not going to pretend I arrived generous. I saw the posters on Thursday and I understood the joke immediately and I thought: he has killed my mother and now he is going to do a bit about her name in a bar.

I went to be angry in the room. That is the truth of why I went.

m_pinawk 81 · 06:52

He spelled it out.

Every letter. Both surnames. He said the tilde out loud.

Four newspapers could not do that. I wrote to two of them. I have the letters. Nobody replied and nobody corrected it and after nine days there was nothing about her anywhere in this city at all, and I have spent four months carrying the fact that my mother died and the record of it has her name wrong.

A man I have every reason to hate stood in a bar and spelled my mother's name letter by letter to three thousand people so they would have it right, and I put my hand over my mouth and I have never in my life had a feeling I could not identify like that.

m_pinawk 81 · 07:20

The joke.

I need to explain this and I am the only person who can and I have been trying to write it since five o'clock this morning.

People made that joke to my mother constantly. For thirty years. At the shelter, at the surgery, at the desk, every new volunteer, every delivery man, the same joke about her name and the drink, over and over, for as long as I have been alive.

And it worked every single time.

She never got tired of it. Not once, not ever. She would laugh properly, every time, like it was the first time, and people kept doing it because of what it did to her face. It was the running joke of her entire life and she loved it and she was in on it and she made it better by loving it.

When I was small I thought it was because she was being polite. I worked out when I was about fifteen that she was not being polite at all. She just thought it was funny. She thought it was funny for thirty years.

That is not written down anywhere. It is not in the four articles. It is not in the obituary because there was not one. It is a thing about my mother that lived in maybe forty people and I am one of them.

He found it. I do not know how. Nobody has asked me anything. Nobody has contacted me at any point.

m_pinawk 81 · 07:41

So here is what I actually watched, at the back, by the door, for ten hours.

I watched a room of three thousand people spend a whole night laughing at my mother's joke. The one she loved. The one nobody has made since October because everybody is frightened of upsetting me.

Nobody has said it to me in four months. My aunt nearly said it at the funeral and stopped herself and the look on her face was the worst part of that whole day.

And in that bar three thousand people did it for ten hours and it was the funniest thing any of them had ever seen and my mother would have been delighted. I am not saying she would have forgiven him. I am saying she would have thought the barbershop one was the best thing that ever happened and she would have made everybody she knew go and see it.

That is who she was. I am not making that up to make this easier on myself. That is just who she was and it is why she was still moving cats out of a building at half past four in the morning at sixty one years old.

m_pinawk 81 · 08:15

And then the last one.

Ninety nine jokes and then he played the song. Properly. No trick in it. Twenty past five in the morning and about a thousand of us left standing.

I cried for the whole of it. I have not cried since the second week and I have been worried about that and so has my husband.

He did not see me. He does not know I was there. I have thought about whether to tell him and I have decided not to, and I have decided not to for a reason I want written down: he did not do it for me. If he had wanted my thanks he could have had it in about four seconds, any day, for four months. He never asked.

He did it for her. For a woman he never met, who is dead because of a clock he put on a screen, who would have liked him, which is the part I can hardly stand.

m_pinawk 81 · 08:30

The last thing and then I am going to go to bed for a long time.

In November I wrote in this guestbook that I was not grateful and that nothing had been made better. People quoted it a lot. It was true when I wrote it.

I am not withdrawing it. My mother is still dead and it is still because of him and no concert changes one second of that, and if anybody in this thread uses what I am about to say to argue that he is a good man I will come back and I will say something I cannot take back.

He is the reason my mother is dead.

He is also the only person in this city who did a single thing about the fact that my mother is dead. Not the papers. Not the council. Not her employer, who she did not have. Not one of them.

I have spent four months trying to make those into one sentence and I have stopped trying, because they are two sentences, and they are both true, and I am done pretending that one of them cancels the other.

I respect him. I have written that word and deleted it eleven times and it is the correct one and I am leaving it.

Thank you to everyone here who has been kind to me. Mr Bloom, thank you for asking me properly, twice, in November. Mrs Okonjo, thank you for what you wrote to me that day.

Her name is Rosario Amador Piña and three thousand people know how to spell it now.

louwk 81

i was forty feet in front of you for ten hours and i had no idea.

im not going to say anything else. this thread belongs to you today and im leaving these six comments at the top of it permanently.

teodora_mwk 81

I am going to say one thing and it is not to Mrs Piña's daughter, it is to this room, and I want it read carefully.

She has said what she has said. It is hers. Nobody in this guestbook gets a vote on it and nobody gets to use it.

I have spent nineteen months insisting that the people who lost somebody are the only ones whose position counts. That has to hold when the position is one I do not share, or it was never a principle, it was just me.

I have not changed my mind about anything. I do not respect him. Elías is still where he is.

And I will fight anybody in this thread who tries to tell that woman she is wrong about her own mother.

mama_okonjowk 81

My dear, I have read your six messages three times and I have had to stop and start.

You have said the thing that I have not been able to say about Chidi for over a year, and you have said it better than I would have, and you are a much younger woman than me.

Two sentences. Both true. Neither cancelling the other. I am going to be thinking about that for a long time.

Your mother sounds like every good woman I have ever known. Thirty years of the same joke and she laughed every time. That is a whole life, that is, right there in one sentence.

doc_wispwk 81

Sixteen weeks of silence, and then this.

I will make one observation and then I am going to stay quiet for a while, because Mrs Piña's daughter has said everything that matters and I do not want to be a clinician on top of it.

In wk 65 he asked a question out loud, in a room, to another person, and was not answered: why do I care about this woman so much.

He has not answered it either. What he has done instead is spend four months finding out who she was, and then spend ten hours and twelve minutes being funny about the thing she found funny.

That is not an answer. It is what a person does when they cannot produce one. And I would note, without drawing any conclusion from it, that it is the first time in nineteen months he has done something at enormous cost that produced no advantage of any kind — no leverage, no demonstration, no audience he needed, no point being made to anybody who could act on it.

He paid for every drink in a bar for ten hours and gave the takings away and left without saying goodnight.

tape_hisswk 81

the song is on the station.

block four. its been there the whole time. i catalogued it with lou in week seventeen and neither of us gave it a second look because its a pop record from 1979 and there are fifty two other things on that list.

hes played that song since before any of us knew he existed. he did not go and get it for this. it was already his.

and the hundredth version is the original. no arrangement. after ninety nine of them he played the thing that was already in the collection, unchanged, correctly, which is the only thing that man has ever done with anything he owns.

ive been telling you for two years what he is. i have never once enjoyed being right until today.

the_quiet_manwk 81

no boards. no broadcast. nothing hacked.

paper, paste and a ladder, in nine districts, by hand.

he owns the ability to put a message on every screen in this city simultaneously and he has used it. for this he went out at night with a bucket.

the takeover was for people who had to be made to listen. this was for people who might want to come.

laundrette_catswk 81

eleven of us went from the shelters. we all knew her, most of us only a bit, but this world is small and she had been in it nine years.

we stood together near the pillar. by about hour four we were doing the joke to each other and by hour six we were doing it to strangers, and a man i had never met bought me a drink he did not have to pay for and said it to me and i laughed like an idiot.

nobody has said her name out loud around me since October without lowering their voice first.

three thousand people shouted it. that is not nothing. i do not know what it is but it is not nothing.

v_did_nothing_wrongwk 81

the look.

i was there and im not going to be able to describe it and lou has already tried and got closer than i will.

three thousand people cheering and he looked at us and we stopped. no hand up. nothing said. two seconds.

and it wasnt fear. thats what ive been trying to explain to people for four days. nobody in that room was frightened. we just all understood at the same moment that we had made it about the wrong person and we were embarrassed.

hes made an entire city do things by threatening it. that is the only time ive ever seen him make a room do something by just being disappointed in it 🥀

shelfstacker_niawk 81

i was on the door end with milk_teeth and about six people from the guestbook and we did not know we were all there until about hour two.

i stayed all ten hours and i was on shift at seven. worth it.

the ambient one was twenty eight minutes and a third of the room left and he played every second of it looking perfectly happy. that is the funniest thing i have ever witnessed in my life.

no_ojoswk 81

i took my abuela. she is eighty six and she has never once come to anything and she asked to go.

she stayed until half eleven, which is five hours, which is four and a half hours past her bedtime. she liked the mariachi one and she did not like the noise one and she said the polka was "correct."

on the way out she said: "he spelled her name. that is what you do for someone when you cannot do anything else. my mother did that at a graveside in 1997 for a woman nobody could bury properly."

and then she said the last thing and im typing it and then im done.

"the candles can go out now. both of them. he has done it himself."

obituary_columnwk 81

Four newspapers reported her death. Three spelled her name wrong. Her daughter wrote to two of them and neither replied.

Sixteen weeks later a man who never met her rented a bar for ten hours, spelled her name out letter by letter to three thousand people, paid for everything they drank, gave the takings to her family, and then played the joke she loved a hundred different ways until five in the morning.

Ninety nine of them were funny. The hundredth was the song, as written, with nothing done to it.

Her daughter stood at the back and was not seen and does not intend to be, and has written six messages this morning in which she says both true things and refuses to reconcile them.

I have been writing endings on this website for two years. That is the only one I have ever read that I could not improve.

nobody should have known i was there.

who's writing this

lou bloom. relay for four and a half months. freelance scene photographer, night shift, mostly watson and heywood. one house, which turns out to have been there the entire time.

this site isnt a job. i want that on record somewhere.

as of wk 17 +7 i own a house, a hypercar, a cat, and a hundred thousand eurodollars with a joke written on them. i have never been paid for a single word on this website.

no contact form. dont ask.
